articles.title: Microsoft unveils Surface Laptop, Pro with new Qualcomm chips
articles.text:
At Snapdragon Summit, which Qualcomm flew me out to, Microsoft unveiled the Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch built on the Snapdragon X2 Plus processor, as well as a new Surface Mouse with integrated haptic feedback.
According to Microsoft, the Snapdragon X2 Plus chipset is up to 17 per cent faster in Office, 18 per cent more efficient in battery performance, 60 per cent faster in graphics performance, and 95 per cent faster in local AI inferencing with the NPU, as it’s capable of 80 TOPS.
The Surface Pro 12-inch is a fanless Windows PC with a 500-nit PixelSense touchscreen that’s 25 per cent brighter than last year’s model. It comes in black, silver, and violet colour variants, though currently it’s not clear if the latter options will come to Canada. The enclosure is made with 86 per cent recycled material. The Surface Pro 12-inch starts at US$1,149.99 ($C1,612) and launches on October 13 in select markets — we’ve reached out for Canadian availability and pricing. Storage options include 256GB and 512GB, and it can have either 16GB or 24GB of RAM.
The Surface Pro 12-inch also offers the new Microsoft Ink Canvas, which is an AI-powered pen experience for sketching, annotating, creating images and summarizing text on the canvas. You’ll be able to download this on October 13.
Now, the 13-inch Surface Laptop, on the other hand, has a full-size backlit keyboard and precision touchpad, alongside an aluminum body, and a taller 500-nit 3:2 PixelSense touchscreen that’s 25 per cent brighter than last year’s model. The laptop offers 22.5 hours of battery life, a pretty violet colour (depending on your market), starts at US$1,199 (C$1,681) and comes out on October 13 — and again, we’ve reached out for Canadian availability and pricing. Storage options include 256GB and 512GB, and it can have either 16GB or 24GB of RAM.
The new Surface Mouse has haptic feedback, which offers a small physical response when performing actions. If you’re clicking, snapping windows into place, and more. Microsoft says that it’s noticeable within seconds, and once you start using it, it’s hard to give up. The Surface Mouse is redesigned for ambidextrous use and has a customizable button for Copilot and other everyday shortcuts. Additionally, it has Bluetooth 6.0, so you can pair it with multiple devices and move between them easily.
I got the opportunity to try out the Surface Mouse at Snapdragon Summit, and I thought the haptics felt pretty good. The company made it so that there’s a physical response whenever there are visual cues. So if you’re dragging and dropping into Outlook and there’s a visual cue, you’ll feel a haptic when you first click on the file, and then when you hover it over Outlook, you’ll feel a different haptic.
Microsoft put together a demo where you can try out the different haptics depending on the activity. One demo had you playing Minesweeper; another had you playing around with your own zen garden, moving rocks around and dragging a rake across the sand. I like that it’s not a general haptic you feel, but changes depending on what you’re doing, even within a single demo.
The haptics aren’t available in everything like gaming, but Microsoft is working with a lot of first-party and third-party apps, such as some of the Adobe suite of apps.
It’s also made with 30 per cent recycled content. The Surface Mouse starts at US$79.99 (about C$112.78) and will be available in Black and Platinum on October 13.

articles.title: Moralischer Kompass: Wie Alignment funktioniert, um KI im Zaum zu halten
articles.text:
Das vertrackte Alignment: Wie KI menschliche Werte lernt – und warum das nicht alles absichern kann
Man kann es für eine PR-Maßnahme halten, oder für echte Sorge: Je mächtiger die Frontier-Modelle der großen KI-Entwickler werden, und je häufiger die Meldungen über erfolgreiche KI-Ausbrüche werden, desto dringlicher werden die Warnungen der KI-Industrie vor ihren eigenen Produkten. Als Beobachter kann man den Eindruck gewinnen, dass zumindest die großen Frontier-Modelle sich nicht mehr kontrollieren lassen und die Orientierung an menschlichen Werten über Bord werfen. Aber wie passt das damit zusammen, wenn doch eigentlich dieselben großen KI-Entwickler:innen ganze Abteilungen betreiben, die genau daran arbeiten: am sogenannten Alignment, also der Ausrichtung an menschlichen und ethischen Richtlinien.

articles.title: Como los Palma DHS-1, pero más económicos: unos auriculares que pasan de abiertos a cerrados con un solo giro y son 'made in Spain'
articles.text:
Los Palma DHS-1 nos llamaron mucho la atención por su particular propuesta de poder elegir si queremos utilizarlos como auriculares abiertos o cerrados, y tras unos años desde su lanzamiento llega una nueva versión mejorada, pero que ve reducido su precio. Los Palma DHS-10 parten de los 1.595 euros en lugar de los 2195 euros que costaba aquel primer modelo.
Unos auriculares que cambian de abiertos a cerrados
Los Palma DHS-10 siguen siendo unos auriculares de gama alta que están orientados a un público audiófilo que busca algo diferente. Y de hecho, esto es uno de los grandes reclamos de este nuevo modelo que, como ya vimos en su predecesor, ofrece la posibilidad de utilizarlos como auriculares abiertos o cerrados dependiendo de la grabación escuchada o de las condiciones del entorno. Para alternar entre estos dos modos basta con girar simultáneamente 14 grados las cubiertas de los cascos.
Esta es su seña de identidad, por lo que es lógico que también la encontremos en un segundo modelo que, afortunadamente, tiene un precio bastante inferior a los DHS-1. Además, como punto diferenciador, Palma Headphones ha cambiado el acabado en madera por un material sintético reciclable de similar geometría para así garantizar que cuentan con la misma ergonomía.
A nivel interno vienen equipados con un transductor electrodinámico con diafragmas de 50 mm y bobina móvil de 26 mm, ofreciendo, según la marca, niveles de presión sonoros muy elevados y sin distorsión.
También cabe señalar que los auriculares incorporan un conectores de 3,5 mm para aumentar las posibilidades de la conexión, ofrecen una baja impedancia (32 ohmios) los auriculares se ensamblan manualmente en Esepaña.
Los auriculares estarán disponibles desde septiembre, hay siete colores diferentes y, como decimos, parten de un precio recomendado de 1.595 euros.

articles.title: How the MSME ODR portal is helping small businesses recover delayed payments
articles.text:
How the MSME ODR portal is helping small businesses recover delayed payments
What happens when a buyer ignores your calls but cannot ignore a council notice
For India's micro and small enterprises (MSEs), getting paid on time is often harder than winning the order. The MSME ODR portal, run by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, is changing how these businesses chase unpaid dues. It lets a small supplier file a claim against a defaulting buyer online, attend conciliation meetings virtually and settle without a lawyer. Accounts from enterprises in Telangana suggest the shift is cutting both the time and the cost of recovery.
Why delayed payments cost small businesses more than money
A delayed payment can hold up salaries, raw material purchases and loan repayments. The MSMED Act, 2006 requires buyers to pay MSE suppliers within 45 days and levies compound interest on defaults. It also lets suppliers refer disputes to a Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council (MSEFC), of which there are 161 across states and Union Territories, according to the Ministry.
In practice, pursuing a claim meant paperwork, trips to the district headquarters and repeated hearings. The Samadhaan portal, launched in 2017, brought filing online but largely worked as a tracking system. For many small suppliers, the effort of recovery outweighed the amount at stake.
How the MSME ODR portal works for small suppliers
The Ministry of MSME is the nodal body behind the platform. The Online Dispute Resolution scheme for delayed payments was launched in December 2023 under RAMP (Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance), a World Bank-supported programme. The portal went live on 27 June 2025, and since 15 October 2025, all new delayed-payment cases must be filed on it.
The portal carries a case from filing to settlement online, covering notices, conciliation meetings and hearings. States continue to run the councils that decide the disputes. In Telangana, the Commissionerate of Industries and Commerce administers six regional MSEFCs through District Industries Centres.
The benefits show up in a casebook compiled by the Commissionerate, which documents enterprises that used the councils. Several report filing online in under an hour, spending less than Rs 1,000 to file, and representing themselves without a lawyer. The most consistent observation is that a formal notice from the council moved buyers who had ignored months of follow-up.
Ankita Pandey, Director, RAMP, Ministry of MSME, writes in the casebook that a delayed-payment dispute is often a commercial relationship under stress. The aim of ODR, she notes, is to enable settlements that let buyers and suppliers keep doing business.
Case studies from the councils
Eminent Engineers, a proprietorship in Medchal-Malkajgiri, had supplied goods to a buyer who defaulted and stopped responding. Proprietor Donga Vasu Sairam filed his claim online in under an hour. The buyer made contact within a week, and the matter was settled in a single conciliation sitting. He estimated savings of around Rs 50,000 in legal costs.
Neemus Software Solutions, based in Ranga Reddy, had several delayed-payment matters pending. According to the Ministry of MSME, it resolved nine of eleven cases through the mechanism, with most respondents choosing not to contest. Director Shalini Agarwal said the route was "cheaper and time-bound versus court", adding that the company would not have approached a court for similar disputes.
For Hyderabad-based PeopleLink Unified Communications, the council has become a routine recovery channel. Its authorised representative filed online and resolved the matter in under a month, the fifth of six recoveries the company has secured this way, as per the casebook.
What the early numbers indicate
Figures shared by the Ministry of MSME in August 2026 indicated that more than 800 cases had been filed in Telangana through the ODR ecosystem, with around 85 resolved. The resolved share is still small, which reflects how recently the platform went live and how long conciliation can take when buyers contest a claim.
How does an MSME file a delayed-payment claim on the ODR portal
A micro or small enterprise with a valid Udyam registration can file once a buyer has not paid within 45 days. The supplier uploads documents such as purchase orders, invoices and proof of delivery, and the claim goes to the facilitation council in its state.
The council first attempts conciliation, with meetings held online. If the parties do not settle, the matter can move to arbitration. The MSMED Act requires a reference to be decided within 90 days, and a buyer who challenges an award in court must first deposit 75% of the awarded amount.
What lies ahead for ODR and small businesses
According to the casebook, the ODR scheme is slated to run through 2026-27, making the coming months a test of whether disposals can keep pace with rising filings. Wider adoption will depend on awareness, since many enterprises in the casebook learnt about the facility through word of mouth or industry associations. If more councils match the speed seen in these cases, the portal could make delayed-payment recovery a routine business process rather than a last resort.

articles.title: Alerte nostalgie : la série d'animation culte Myster Mask va revenir sur Disney+
articles.text:
Alerte nostalgie : la série d'animation culte Myster Mask va revenir sur Disney+
Let's get dangerous (again)
En développement depuis plusieurs années, le reboot du dessin animé culte Darkwing Duck (Myster Mask en VF) va bel et bien voir le jour sur la plateforme de streaming Disney+, avec de premiers détails qui donnent envie.
Disney a décidément le chic pour souffler le chaud et le froid avec sa plateforme Disney+. Après l'annonce de l'annulation de Daredevil: Born Again après trois saisons, ce 22 septembre il est question d'une très bonne nouvelle : le retour de la série d'animation Darkwing Duck (Myster Mask en VF).
Un grand héros et une équipe qui va vous en boucher un coin
Diffusée pour la première fois en 1991 et très populaire en France sur le Disney Club, cette parodie assumée de Batman faisant intervenir des personnages de DuckTales (La Bande à Picsou) suivait les aventures de super-héros combattant du crime Darkwing Duck, dont l'alter ego se nommait Drake Mallard. Après une seule saison de 91 épisodes (!), le comédien de doublage Jim Cummings (Gérard Hernandez chez nous) rangera finalement son costume.
Annoncé il y a quelques années après la fin du solide reboot de DuckTales, ce projet de retour est désormais officiellement validé par Disney+. La nouvelle série sera écrite par Sean Tretta (Star Trek: Picard) et Borja Peña Gorostegui (Lost & Crowned), tandis que Tad Stones, créateur de la série originale, sera consultant.
- Le teaser de la nouvelle série Myster Mask :
Un synopsis est même de sortie pour ce retour : “Depuis 35 ans, Darkwing Duck est prisonnier de son pire cauchemar : un monde parallèle qui ignore tout de ses exploits de super-héros. Mais une adolescente rebelle prénommée Duckie, qui connaît parfaitement son passé héroïque, surgit pour ramener au combat ce justicier à l’ego surdimensionné. Ensemble, ce duo improbable devra prendre tous les risques pour affronter d’anciens ennemis tels que Negaduck et Megavolt, et retrouver ses alliés (Flagada Jones, Poussinette et Morgana) afin de sauver l’univers tout entier.”
	
Comme tous les autres fans de la série originale, j'ai hâte de voir Darkwing se lancer à nouveau dans des aventures périlleuses (*getting dangerous again*, ndlr) dans une toute nouvelle série.
Le casting vocal commence également à se dessiner, et il donne déjà envie d'y être. Mark Hamill sera Darkwing Duck, tandis que Seth Rogen, également à la production exécutive, sera Launchpad McQuack (Flagada Jones). De plus, Lizzy Caplan sera Poussinette Canardstein (Gosalyn Waddlemeyer) et Lilimar sera Duckie. Dan Stevens, Tiffany Shepis, Kathryn Newton, Teo Briones, Tyler Dean Flores, Katie Rich et Nat Faxon ont aussi été annoncés.
En attendant ce retour qui promet “plus d'action et de comédie sans oublier le cœur Disney”, outre la série originale, n'hésitez pas sur Disney+ à vous jeter sur le formidable reboot de DuckTales, où le personnage faisait déjà plus ou moins une apparition, doublé par Chris Diamantopoulos. Let's get dangerous (again).

articles.title: Apple préparerait un bracelet fitness sans écran pour rivaliser avec Whoop et Oura
articles.text:
Selon Bloomberg, Apple développerait un bracelet de suivi santé dépourvu d’écran, actuellement en phase d’étude technologique précoce, mais ne serait probablement pas commercialisé avant 2028, si Apple décide finalement de le poursuivre.
Longtemps considérée comme l’un des acteurs majeurs des objets connectés dédiés à la santé, l’Apple Watch fait aujourd’hui face à une concurrence qui grandit vite et autrement : des trackers minimalistes, sans le moindre écran, entièrement tournés vers le suivi biométrique continu. Whoop, valorisée autour de 10 milliards de dollars et qui envisage elle aussi une entrée en Bourse, ou encore Oura, qui vient de déposer son dossier d’introduction en Bourse, ont su fédérer des millions d’utilisateurs avec cette approche épurée. Apple, selon Bloomberg, explore à son tour cette catégorie avec un projet encore loin d’être finalisé.
Un bracelet en tissu, qui suscite l’intérêt de Tim Cook et Eddy Cue
Les prototypes actuellement étudiés se présenteraient sous la forme d’un bracelet en tissu fin, relié à un module électronique compact équipé de capteurs, chargé de mesurer le rythme cardiaque et d’autres indicateurs physiologiques. Le dispositif reprendrait ainsi une partie des fonctions de suivi de l’Apple Watch, mais sans écran, afin de limiter les notifications envoyées à l'utilisateur. Le projet en resterait pour l’instant au stade de l’étude technologique, une phase précoce qui ne garantit en rien sa commercialisation future.
Ce dossier suscite d’ailleurs l’intérêt de deux figures de poids chez Apple : Tim Cook, désormais président exécutif de l’entreprise, et Eddy Cue, responsable des services, qui a pris la tête de la division santé fin 2025 après le départ à la retraite de Jeff Williams. Toujours selon Bloomberg, Cue pousse notamment les équipes santé d’Apple à s’intéresser à des produits aux interfaces plus simples, à l’image de ceux proposés par Whoop et Oura, plutôt que de chercher à multiplier les fonctions.
Ce chantier intervient dans un contexte de recomposition au sein des équipes santé et montre connectée d’Apple, avec les départs récents de Stan Ng, ancien responsable marketing de l'Apple Watch, et de Jay Blahnik, qui dirigeait les initiatives fitness de la marque.
Une influence déjà visible sur l’Apple Watch actuelle
Apple a déjà intégré à ses dernières Apple Watch et à l’application Santé plusieurs fonctions similaires à celles proposées par Whoop et Oura, notamment un score de préparation quotidien ou une estimation de l’âge biologique. Ces évolutions témoignent de l’importance croissante accordée par Apple au suivi global de la santé, au-delà du seul suivi sportif.
Google s’est également positionné sur ce créneau du tracker sans écran avec le lancement du Google Fitbit Air, tandis que d’autres acteurs comme Garmin sont déjà présents sur le marché des objets dédiés au suivi de la santé et de l’activité physique.
La publication du rapport de Bloomberg a par ailleurs eu un effet immédiat sur Garmin : l’action du fabricant a reculé jusqu’à 2,5 % en séance, selon Bloomberg. Cette réaction intervient alors qu’Apple explore précisément un marché sur lequel Garmin est déjà présent.
Même en cas de feu vert définitif, ce bracelet sans écran ne serait probablement pas commercialisé avant 2028. Apple dispose donc encore de plusieurs années pour poursuivre ses essais, modifier le concept ou, comme cela arrive régulièrement avec les projets exploratoires de l’entreprise, décider finalement de ne pas le commercialiser.

articles.title: YouTube vai deixar você criar feeds próprios na página inicial • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
YouTube vai deixar você criar feeds próprios na página inicial
Novidade permite criar abas com vídeos sobre temas escolhidos. Recurso chega ao celular e desktop em outubro.
O YouTube vai permitir que usuários criem feeds personalizados na página inicial. A partir do mês que vem, um nova opção aparecerá na parte superior da plataforma, na qual será possível clicar e descrever em texto o tipo de conteúdo que você quer acompanhar.
A novidade foi apresentada pela executiva Emily Moxley, vice-presidente de gerenciamento de produtos de Viewer AI, durante coletiva de imprensa acompanhada pelo Tecnoblog. “Os feeds personalizados permitem criar abas dedicadas na página inicial para qualquer interesse”, afirmou.
Na prática, o usuário poderá escrever algo como “podcasts para meu trajeto de 30 minutos”, exemplo citado por Moxley. A aba será atualizada automaticamente com novos vídeos.
Essa novidade será viabilizada através da busca por chat com inteligência artificial, que estava sendo testada há meses. O recurso Ask YouTube (aquele botão “Perguntar” logo abaixo do vídeo) também terá uma função de guia de compras integrada: ao pesquisar um produto, o usuário vai receber uma tabela comparativa com informações reunidas a partir de outros vídeos na plataforma. Com isso, o YouTube passa a concentrar tarefas que antes poderiam levar os clientes à Busca do Google.
O recurso se soma à chegada da Amazon ao programa de afiliados da plataforma no Brasil. A partir de hoje, criadores brasileiros poderão marcar produtos vendidos pela varejista em seus vídeos e receber comissão pelas vendas geradas.
Segundo o gerente-geral do YouTube Shopping, Travis Katz, o programa já reúne 1,3 milhão de criadores afiliados e multiplicou por 13 o volume de vendas gerado por eles nos últimos dois anos. De acordo com o executivo, as “pessoas assistem a 110 milhões de horas de vídeos relacionados a compras no YouTube todos os dias”.
O YouTube também anunciou dublagem automática para transmissões ao vivo. O recurso ainda está em testes e, inicialmente, vai funcionar entre inglês e espanhol, mas a dublagem automática já é usada pelo YouTube em vídeos publicados na plataforma e foi ampliada para 27 idiomas em 2026.
A executiva Aparna Pappu, vice-presidente de gerenciamento de produtos das áreas de criação, afirmou que a ferramenta tenta atender ao crescimento da audiência internacional das lives: mais de 40% do tempo assistido em transmissões ao vivo vem de espectadores que estão fora do país do criador, segundo dados do YouTube.
A empresa oficializou as novidades no evento anual Made On YouTube, que acontece em Nova York nesta quarta-feira (23/09).

articles.title: Cuál es el cable HDMI 2.2 para televisores y por qué no se debe comprar hoy para conectar un Smart TV
articles.text:
La empresa Silkland se convirtió en la primera marca en abrir pedidos del cable HDMI 2.2 Ultra96, una nueva generación de conectores que duplica el ancho de banda máximo disponible hasta ahora, pasando de 48 a 96 gigabits por segundo.
Aunque esta tecnología ya empieza a estar disponible, todavía no es el momento de acceder a ella, mientras el resto de la industria se adapta a este estándar, como sucedió con el HDMI 2.1.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo es el cable HDMI 2.2 y qué mejora en el TV
Antes de hablar de por qué no conviene comprarlo todavía, vale entender qué es y por qué importa. Un cable HDMI es el conector que une el televisor con aparatos como consolas de videojuegos, reproductores o computadoras. La versión del cable determina qué tan buena puede ser la imagen y el sonido que viajan por esa conexión.
La versión 2.2, cuya especificación técnica fue aprobada oficialmente en junio de 2025, amplía de forma considerable esa capacidad. Con 96 Gbps de ancho de banda —el doble que su predecesor—, puede transmitir video en 4K a 240 cuadros por segundo sin comprimir, y en 8K a 60 cuadros por segundo con todos los colores completos. Si se activan ciertas configuraciones de compresión, las cifras escalan aún más: 8K a 240 Hz, o incluso resoluciones de 16K.
PUBLICIDAD
En términos prácticos esto significa que más ancho de banda permite tener imágenes más fluidas, colores más fieles y, sobre todo, menos posibilidades de que la conexión sea el eslabón débil de un sistema de entretenimiento de alta gama.
La nueva versión también incluye una función llamada Protocolo de Indicación de Latencia (LIP, por sus siglas en inglés), que permite que los dispositivos conectados —como una barra de sonido o un amplificador— se comuniquen entre sí para sincronizar mejor el audio con el video, un problema frecuente en sistemas de cine en casa con múltiples aparatos encadenados.
Por qué todavía no es el momento de comprar un HDMI 2.2
El problema central es que aunque los cables existen, los dispositivos que podrían sacarles provecho todavía no han llegado, según Pocket-lint.
Las tarjetas de video más modernas disponibles hoy —la serie GeForce RTX 50 de NVIDIA y la serie Radeon RX 9000 de AMD— utilizan la versión anterior del conector, HDMI 2.1b. Lo mismo ocurre con los modelos actuales de Intel. Ninguna placa gráfica en el mercado soporta HDMI 2.2.
PUBLICIDAD
El panorama en televisores es igual. A la fecha, ningún fabricante, ni LG, ni Sony, ni Samsung, ofrece un modelo con este puerto. Marcas que antes apostaban fuerte por la resolución 8K han dado marcha atrás ante la escasa demanda del público, en parte porque el contenido disponible en esa calidad es casi inexistente.
Las primeras tarjetas de video compatibles con HDMI 2.2 no llegarían antes de 2027. Según versiones sin confirmar, la arquitectura RDNA 5 de AMD estaría diseñada para soportar la nueva versión, aunque solo hasta 80 Gbps, no los 96 Gbps completos. NVIDIA no ha confirmado si su futura serie RTX 60 adoptará el estándar.
PUBLICIDAD
El escenario actual recuerda al de quien compra un accesorio de última generación para un dispositivo que aún no existe. Los cables son retrocompatibles, funcionan perfectamente en televisores y consolas actuales, pero su capacidad adicional no tiene ningún uso real hoy, ni en el corto plazo.
La llegada del HDMI 2.1 al mercado de consumo tardó cerca de dos años desde su aprobación oficial. Con el 2.2, el patrón podría repetirse: los primeros televisores con este puerto podrían aparecer hacia fines de 2026, y la utilidad real del cable podría no materializarse hasta después de 2027.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: This guy has spent two years hunting fake job listings on LinkedIn, and found 60,000 of them
articles.text:
Big quote: Verified profiles, company pages, and polished job listings are being used to lure job seekers into scams that can cost them money or expose their personal information. Jay Jones, a Chicago-area job seeker who calls himself The Profiler, has made it his mission to find them. Since being laid off from an advertising role in late 2023, Jones says he has helped get nearly 60,000 fake job listings removed from the internet, most of them from LinkedIn. He has also flagged about 7,000 profiles that he believes were used in job scams.
The fraud is not limited to obvious fake accounts. Some scammers create batches of recruiter profiles using copied photos and similar account details. Others take over dormant, verified LinkedIn accounts and attach them to legitimate companies. Still others place job ads on legitimate company pages that direct applicants to outside websites or email addresses.
The approach is becoming increasingly sophisticated. Jones said scammers use artificial intelligence to tailor job pitches to a person's résumé or career history. A recruiter might tell an applicant that their résumé needs work and then offer to help for a fee. Other scams seek more valuable information, including a driver's license or Social Security number.
Jones recently came across several LinkedIn accounts using the name Linda Anthony. The accounts used the same image, showed recent creation dates, and listed similar roles at "Confidential Jobs." One profile described Linda Anthony as a contract recruiter in Smyrna, Ga., while another identified her as a contract specialist in California.
Jones said the profile URLs also appeared to follow the same pattern, suggesting the accounts had been created in bulk. After he posted about them online, the links went dark.
Image credit: The Wall Street Journal
"You turn the lights on," he told The Wall Street Journal, "and the roaches run."
The scams are landing at a difficult time for people looking for work. In August, 27% of unemployed Americans had been searching for a job for more than six months, near the highest level in more than a decade outside the pandemic.
LinkedIn said its automated systems stop most scam activity before users see it. The company said it blocked nearly 90 million fake accounts before they went live in the second half of 2025. It has also introduced new safety features and worked with the FBI this summer to educate job seekers about scams.
Still, the platform faces a persistent problem: fake accounts and fake listings can borrow credibility from real people and real companies.
One scheme Jones has tracked involves hijacked LinkedIn accounts. Some users verify their identities on the platform, receive a verification badge, and later stop using their profiles. Scammers can take control of those accounts, change the work history, and list the account holder as a recruiter for a legitimate business.
That can give a scammer a verified profile and a company affiliation at the same time.
Jones found several such accounts listed as employees of Argenta Talent Acquisition, a Colorado recruiting firm. One account belonged to a dentist in Chile. Argenta CEO Kelley Barcus said the bogus profiles created a direct threat to her company.
"It's my brand, it's my reputation," she said.
Barcus hired Jones to get the accounts disconnected from Argenta's LinkedIn page. LinkedIn accepted reports on the profiles, but the accounts had 14 days to update their information or appeal before LinkedIn could remove their company affiliation. LinkedIn said that process can help correct inaccurate employment information.
Jones said the delay gave scammers more time to reach job seekers. "Scammers don't deserve fairness," he said. "It's economic terrorism."
Oscar Rodriguez, LinkedIn's vice president of trust product, said scammers adapt quickly as platforms add new defenses. LinkedIn asks recruiters to verify their identities, but Rodriguez said verification doesn't guarantee that a profile or job posting is legitimate.
The company plans to introduce a tool later this month that would allow verified employers to immediately remove users' affiliations with their companies.
Jones also looks for fraud inside legitimate company pages. In one case, he found what appeared to be 30 job listings on Hyundai Motor's verified LinkedIn page. The positions included data-entry specialist and customer-service representative. Screenshots reviewed by The Wall Street Journal showed that the ads contained errors and linked to an outside site not affiliated with Hyundai. Applicants were told to email résumés to an outside address.
He found a similar issue involving Capital One. Job ads for administrative assistants appeared on LinkedIn but led to an unaffiliated website. Jones compared the listings with Capital One's own career site, where similar openings were generally listed under titles such as senior administrative assistant or administrative assistant III.
Hyundai and Capital One said they work with LinkedIn to remove fraudulent job postings.
For Jones, the work has become more than a side project. He still searches for a permanent job, drives for Uber, and trains cybersecurity professionals to recognize scam tactics. He also seeks paid speaking work, raises money online, and sells apparel with anti-scam slogans.
He often keeps about 50 browser tabs open while tracking leads, he said, and his browser crashes several times a week.

articles.title: Counter-Strike 2 Gets New Rush Game Mode With 40 Second, 3v3 Rounds
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 23rd 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Counter-Strike 2 Gets New Rush Game Mode With 40 Second, 3v3 Rounds
Counter-Strike 2 just received a rare, sizeable content update that both introduces a brand-new game mode and makes several tweaks and changes to how the game works, looks, and feels. The biggest change to Counter-Strike 2 is the new Rush game mode, which is a "fast-paced 3v3 queued mode," that puts players through a series of 40-second-long matches on randomly selected arenas specifically designed for the shorter games. 
Terrorists and Counter-Terrorists will effectively face off against one another in king of the hill-style matches, in which the objective is to control a point until time runs out or eliminate the enemy before time runs out. The team with the most rounds won at the end of the game is the winner, and Valve has added a custom Rush leaderboard to specifically track performance and compare to friends.Another notable change that came in the update is a new selection process for Premier matches. Under the new system, each team votes to select two maps each, and then a map is randomly selected from the four finalists. This seems to be an attempt to allow teams a little more control over the map selection—compared to the previous ban system—and have a chance at playing on a map for which they have developed gameplay strategies.
The update also reworks blood and bullet impacts so that "blood is now much more bloody, and bullet impacts are far more impacty," effectively giving players better visual indication of a hit or a miss. There are also new crosshair customization options, including new shapes, updated color, transparency, and thickness options.

articles.title: Owners mourn spoiled food after firmware update bricks Samsung smart fridges
articles.text:
Some Samsung smart fridges stopped working on Tuesday due to a firmware update.
Korean outlets were the first to report the problems, which affect Samsung’s Bespoke AI line of fridges. Star News Korea, per a Google-provided translation, said that most of the affected devices were four-door fridges from 2024 or later.
Affected fridges “suddenly lost power and stopped functioning immediately after” trying to issue a firmware update through SmartThings, Samsung’s smart home platform, per Star News Korea. The SmartThings app then showed the devices as offline. Some users said that their fridge’s internal display was stuck showing the message “Checking SmartThings app during update.”
There are numerous reports on Samsung’s Korean community forum detailing the problem. Some users claim that they have owned their affected fridge for just a year or less.
“[T]he refrigeration and refrigeration functions themselves did not work normally, so all the food in the refrigerator had to be disposed of,” one user wrote, per a translation.
Samsung didn’t respond to Ars’ questions about what it will do to prevent this from happening in the future or how many units are affected and in which countries. SBS Korea reported that customers have filed hundreds of cases.
The complaints seem to originate only from Korea, where the problem has been made worse because it’s happening during a major Korean holiday, Chuseok, which celebrates the autumn harvest and starts Thursday.
“Customers only trusted Samsung Electronics and made an official update, but it is so absurd and embarrassing that they can’t even use refrigeration and refrigeration functions before the Chuseok,” a forum user wrote, per a Google-provided translation.

articles.title: NextLM brings its precision prospecting agent to Google Cloud Marketplace - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
NextLM brings its precision prospecting agent to Google Cloud Marketplace
NextLM Inc., which makes software that uses behavioral analysis and custom artificial intelligence models to help sales professionals identify and rank individual sales leads, is bringing its AI Prospecting Agent to Google LLC’s Cloud Marketplace and Gemini Enterprise.
The New York-based startup says its agent analyzes behavioral signals, identifies individuals it believes are researching a customer’s product and shows sellers the activity behind each recommendation. Customers can purchase the service using existing Google Cloud spending commitments and invoke the agent within Gemini Enterprise.
The distinction between company-level and individual-level intent is central to NextLM’s pitch. Business-to-business sellers typically have little visibility into who is researching their company and market. That makes prospecting a fishing expedition as salespeople try to identify the people behind a visitor’s IP address.
NextLM says its data engine processes 35 billion behavioral signals daily and spans more than 300 million companies and 370 million professional profiles. Chief Executive Chris Anzalone tol SiliconANGLE the company draws on advertising platforms and public databases to connect activity with individuals. Its model looks for combinations of behavior that may indicate an impending purchase.
“It’s not the specifics of the signals. It’s the way they interrelate with each other,” Anzalone said. Someone browsing a real estate site, for example, may simply be curious. Research into schools and restaurants in the same area provides stronger evidence of a likely home buyer.
The agent presents only prospects in the top 10% of its scores, Anzalone said. Each customer also gets a private adaptation of NextLM’s model that learns from its own sales wins and losses. The company says it doesn’t use customers’ deal data to retrain the shared base model.
Custom model
The service uses Savant, a lightweight AI model built on top of Nvidia Corp.’s Nemotron architecture that NextLM has fine-tuned for prospect scoring. NextLM says it trained the model on Nvidia DGX Spark systems and serves it on Nvidia A100 graphics processing units hosted on Google Cloud. Sellers can use the agent directly in Gemini Enterprise or feed its results into workflows built with Google’s Agent Designer.
In a company-published benchmark, NextLM reported that Savant delivered a 2.45-fold improvement in capturing eventual buyers among its highest-scored prospects compared with nine general-purpose AI models. It also reported a scoring cost of between 3 cents and 11 cents per thousand prospects when running on an owned GPU, which it said is an order of magnitude less than frontier models.
Anzalone said early customer results suggest that about one in four recommended prospects either closes or advances to an open opportunity that appears likely to close within 60 to 90 days. That measure combines completed sales with opportunities still in progress, and Anzalone said NextLM has not amassed enough data to assess how consistently the result holds across all customers.
Identifying named people from online behavior naturally raises questions about accuracy and privacy. Anzalone acknowledged that NextLM cannot match every person to the activity it observes. “There’s lots of people we can’t identify,” he said. “The ones we can identify with a high degree of certainty are the ones that we surface in the platform.”
NextLM applies an internal compliance checklist, relies on assurances from its data partners about consent and excludes users covered by Europe’s General Data Protection Regulation. The company only passes along the name of prospects who demonstrate a 97% likelihood to buy based on its scoring criteria.
The company’s lowest-priced plan starts at $599 a month without a long-term contract, with credits consumed as customers request prospects and related research.
Anzalone said Google integration makes NextLM easier to obtain and use within a broader workflow. While the company is open to working with other cloud providers, “With how good Google has been to us, we don’t have any intentions to move our infrastructure elsewhere,” he said.

articles.title: I tested Huawei's new blood pressure-monitoring watch with a real inflatable cuff inside its strap, and its the best option yet for this health measurement
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
There’s no escaping the fact that the Huawei Watch D3 is an impressive piece of kit. To be able to offer blood pressure monitoring, pulse wave arrhythmia analysis, beat-by-beat ECG, and arterial stiffness detection in a smartwatch is impressive. The mechanical airbag is a little uncomfortable, and an edge-to-edge display would look better, but considering the D3 is targeted at medical-conscious users, Huawei should be praised for what they’ve created.
Pros
- +Blood pressure monitoring
- +Attractive design
- +Rotating crown button
- +NFC payments
Cons
- -Bulky strap
- -Uncomfortable rear sensor plate
- -Display is not edge to edge
Why you can trust TechRadar
Huawei Watch D3: One minute review
It’s been two years since the release of the Huawei Watch D2, and the Chinese brand has decided it’s time to offer an upgraded model, aptly named the D3. With the D range, Huawei was the first to introduce blood pressure monitoring capabilities in a smartwatch, providing a simple way to track the important health metric without needing a dedicated monitor.
In my Huawei Watch D2 review I gave the smartwatch an impressive 4.5 stars. I had high praise for the blood pressure monitoring and clever strap but was left underwhelmed by the bulky design, high price tag, and lack of smartwatch features. Huawei has gone some way to address these concerns, but not universally and in some ways not enough. As a result, the D3 isn’t yet one of the best smartwatches around, but as a medical-first device, it approaches and blends the lifestyle and medical aspects well.
The D3 is primarily a medical device rather than one of the best fitness trackers or running watches. That’s evidenced by its CE-MDR certification that is proudly presented on the watch’s product page. Its commitment to medical reporting means that at times Huawei is forced to prioritize function over form. This is the case with the blood pressure monitoring.
To be able to offer ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, the D3 has to feature a mechanical airbag and pressure sensor. This is attached to the inside of the strap, and even though Huawei has narrowed the thickness of the airbag compared to the D2, it still lacks the comfort of most other smartwatches that don’t have this onboard hardware.
In testing I didn’t have time to compare the D3 against a dedicated blood pressure cuff, but I was able to check it was in the same range as my expectations. The watch takes less than a minute to carry out the check, and all you have to do is place the watch at the same height as your heart and remain still.
Because single measurements are insufficient to determine trends, I used the auto-reminder feature to alert me so I didn’t forget to capture regular measurements. After doing this for several days, I was able to see how my blood pressure changed depending on the time of day and what my average performance was. In addition to this, it’s possible to easily generate a report to share with your GP from within the Huawei Health app.
Blood pressure monitoring is the D3’s magic trick, but the watch offers other health tracking, including pulse wave arrhythmia analysis and beat-by-beat ECG. During testing, I experienced repeated poor signal issues with the ECG measurements, but the arrhythmia analysis worked perfectly.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
While I was working through the health metrics, I strapped on a dedicated heart rate monitor so I could carry out an independent comparison. Both devices reported identical rates, although the D3 was slightly slower to adjust to changes. Finding each health metric is simple and straightforward thanks to the rotating crown control, and the interface clearly guides you through the required steps to perform each one.
Huawei has worked hard to reduce the bulk of the watch, stripping off 2mm from the watch thickness and bringing it down to just 11.3mm. That’s pretty impressive, but unfortunately this measurement doesn’t take into consideration the sensor, which protrudes out the bottom, and despite its smooth surface, feels a little uncomfortable on the wrist.
The watch features an enlarged 1.92-inch AMOLED display with 3000 nits of peak brightness. It is colorful, vibrant, and looks fantastic, offering the same excellent visibility when used both inside and out. Unfortunately, there’s still a significant black strip between the edge of the display and the surrounding case, which results in a lot of dead space. An edge-to-edge display would look far better.
The D3 prioritizes medical reporting, but it also offers over 100 workout modes and a generous range of smart features, including notifications, Bluetooth calling, NFC payments, and voice note recording. These elevate the usefulness of the watch and make it a handy companion for everyday life.
I said earlier that I had an issue with the price of the D2, and Huawei has done nothing to make the D3 more affordable. In fact, it’s £50 more than its predecessor was at launch. The only thing that softens the blow is that if you purchase the watch before September 22, 2027, then you’ll get 10 months of Bupa Well+ health services.
It’s hard to get away from the fact that the D3 is focused on a very niche market. If you’re concerned about your blood pressure or would simply like to keep an eye on it, then the D3 is the perfect solution. The trade-off is a watch that is bulkier and slightly more uncomfortable than most other smartwatches of this size, but we have to give the D3 credit: when even Apple Watches are focused on hypertension detection via LEDs, Huawei continues to back its unique cuff-based solution.
Huawei Watch D3: Specifications
| Component | Huawei Watch D3 | 
| Price | £399 | 
| Dimensions | 46.5 × 41mm and 11.3mm thick | 
| Weight | 40g without strap | 
| Case/bezel | Aluminium alloy | 
| Display | 1.92 inch AMOLED (408 × 480 pixels, PPI 328) | 
| GPS | No | 
| Battery life | 1 day with the ABPM feature enabled or 6 days without | 
| Connection | Bluetooth and NFC | 
| Water resistance | No | 
Huawei Watch D3: Scorecard
| Category | Comment | Score | 
| Value | A mid-range smartwatch where you’re paying for the advanced blood pressure monitoring feature. | 4/5 | 
| Design | A modern, good-looking smartwatch that is only let down by its bulk. | 4/5 | 
| Features | Capable of recording an impressive set of medical-related metrics with workout modes and smart features to boot. | 4/5 | 
| Performance | Reliably accurate results with blood pressure recordings within my expected range. Heart rate measurements were spot on. | 4/5 | 
Huawei Watch D3: Should I buy?
Buy it if...
You need a convenient way to track your blood pressure at home
It takes just one minute per test, and the app generates an exportable report that you can take to your GP.
You’re interested in more medical-related metrics
With pulse wave arrhythmia analysis and beat-by-beat ECG, the Huawei D3 offers more than most watches in this area.
Don't buy it if...
You have no interest in blood pressure monitoring
There are better smartwatches at this price point that offer a more well-rounded smartwatch experience.
You want a fitness tracker
If you’re a fitness enthusiast or runner, then a dedicated watch for these purposes will serve you better.
Also consider
Huawei Band 11 Pro
A better all-round fitness tracker that’s significantly more affordable. It also offers some medical measurements, including arrhythmia analysis and sleep apnea monitoring, but no blood pressure.
Read our Huawei Band 11 Pro review
Apple Watch Series 11
Apple Watches feature a 'hypertension detection' feature, that can indicate trends over 30 days, but not instant blood pressure readings like Huawei's cuff.
Read our Apple Watch Series 11 review
How I tested the Huawei Watch D3
I wore the D3 for 72 hours, and during this time I performed every medical test that the watch offers. Despite not having time to compare the blood pressure results to a dedicated monitor, I was able to compare the heart rate readings to a heart rate monitor. I also used the D3 to keep on top of my notifications, check the weather, and record some voice notifications.
First reviewed: September 2026
Writer, app-hoarder, and professional "low battery" enthusiast. Paul spends his days testing wearables so you don’t have to, and his nights wondering if his sleep tracker is judging him. He’s fascinated by the tech that claims to make us better humans—and if it’s wearable, downloadable, or requires a firmware update, he has thoughts on it.
With over 20 years of experience and a first-class Computer Science degree, Paul has navigated the front lines of the tech and creative industries. His work has been published internationally and appears regularly in Digital Camera World and Creative Bloq.

articles.title: If Amazon doesn’t know how to eliminate carbon emissions, then who does? | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Amazon’s chief sustainability officer said Tuesday the company doesn’t know how it will achieve its goal of net-zero carbon emissions by 2040.
“We are still striving towards that target,” Kara Hurst said at an Axios event, adding later that she is “not going to sit here and say, ‘We know all the ways that we’re going to do this.’”
The admission was both frank and realistic. It’s also a bit disappointing. If Amazon doesn’t have a plan to decarbonize, then who does?
Amazon is one of the largest companies in the world, with last year’s revenue up 12% to $717 billion — about the size of Ireland’s economy. Its rise is illustrative of how, as UN Secretary General António Guterres has pointed out, power has shifted from governments to a few corporations.
As power moves, responsibility follows. The question is, how much responsibility does Amazon bear?
“This isn’t a question of companies versus governments,” Hurst told TechCrunch in a written reply to questions after the event. “Tackling climate change at the scale it demands takes both, and it takes them working together.” She added, “Where we can lead, we do.”
It’s true that Amazon has not been sitting still. In her talk yesterday, Hurst pointed out that the company is “one of the largest purchasers of clean energy in the world for the last several years running” with 42 gigawatts in its portfolio. She also said that Amazon has reduced its carbon intensity, or how much pollution it generates per dollar of revenue, though that claim depends on the time frame. Last year, carbon intensity rose compared with 2024, even though it stayed below where it was in 2022.
Amazon is a sprawling business, and as a result, its carbon emissions are spread across nearly every sector of the economy, from aviation and AI to agriculture and construction. The company needs suppliers in every sector to achieve its goal. “This is not something we can do alone,” Hurst said at the Axios event.
The company acknowledges that its commitments are its own. “We hold ourselves accountable to The Climate Pledge goal of net-zero carbon by 2040. That commitment hasn’t changed,” Hurst told TechCrunch.
But Amazon has also made choices that undermine its leadership on the issue. Earlier this year, an investigation revealed the company’s plans to build a 7.65 gigawatt natural gas power plant to power an AI data center campus. The project’s 35 turbines could release up to 33 million tons of carbon dioxide annually, making it the largest single source of that pollution in the U.S.
With few exceptions, companies prioritize revenue growth over climate commitments. For a company like Amazon, which operates the largest cloud service in the world, AI is apparently a revenue driver that’s impossible to pass up.
The climate tech world has been hoping that, as clean power gets cheaper, the market would work its magic to lower carbon emissions. There have been a few success stories, but as the AI rush has shown, that approach has its limits. Even Amazon, one of the leaders in the space, bet big on natural gas. In the process, it essentially said that climate change is something for future generations of executives to deal with. Sound familiar?

articles.title: "Impressive level of openness": Xiaomi goes way beyond the usual open-weight playbook with MiMo-V2.6
articles.text:
“Impressive level of openness”: Xiaomi goes way beyond the usual open-weight playbook with MiMo-V2.6
New models are coming out thick and fast, almost on a weekly cadence, ranging from the powerful proprietary systems coming out of the major US AI labs to the more open alternatives being released by some of China’s biggest tech companies.
On Tuesday alone, Anthropic debuted Claude Opus 5.5, while OpenAI launched GPT-6 Sol and Luna, each accompanied by their the usual claims about how they outperform their rivals. Amidst all the hullabaloo of the frontier-model frenzy, however, Xiaomi also debuted MiMo-V2.6, another powerful open model from one of China’s growing ranks of AI developers.
All the initial headline numbers look pretty promising, too. The flagship MiMo-V2.6-Pro is a trillion-parameter model, with 42 billion parameters active at a time, a one-million-token context window, and support for text, images, audio and video. Broadly speaking, that puts it in the same frontier territory as the latest models from OpenAI and Anthropic: GPT-6 Sol has a 1.05-million-token context window, while Claude Opus 5.5 has a one-million-token window, though neither company discloses comparable parameter counts.
Xiaomi, for its part, makes broad claims of frontier-level performance across coding, agentic tasks, cybersecurity, multimodal work and research. Independent analysis lends some weight to those claims –Artificial Analysis gives MiMo-V2.6-Pro an Intelligence Index score of 46, ranking it first among the 114 large open-weight models it tracks.
So far, so good. But arguably the bigger story in Xiaomi’s offering is the manner in which it trained the model, how much of that process it showed in public, and what it’s releasing afterward.
A public record
Xiaomi livestreamed its RL training through a public dashboard, exposing metrics from the production reinforcement-learning runs in real time over a five-day period starting on September 15. By the time the runs had finished, the dashboard showed costs of $854,044 for the smaller MiMo-V2.6-Flash model and $2,620,670 for Pro — about $3.5 million combined.
It’s worth noting that this figure covers only the RL stage; Xiaomi hasn’t said what pretraining the models cost. Even so, public RL bills are rare. The closest precedents came last year, when MiniMax said the RL phase of its 456-billion-parameter MiniMax-M1 cost $534,700 in GPU rental, and DeepSeek put the RL training of its 671-billion-parameter R1 at $294,000. Both were leading open reasoning models when they launched, though the comparison only goes so far: MiMo-V2.6-Pro is larger, and its RL run targeted longer, agentic tasks.
Shortly after the stream began, Fuli Luo, who leads Xiaomi’s MiMo team after previously working at DeepSeek, took to X to explain the thinking behind the project. The team, she said, had spent almost six months exploring how far RL could be pushed, increasing the amount of training, the variety of environments and agent setups, and the resources used to grade the model’s attempts.
“We’ll open-source the details piece by piece over the coming weeks,” she added.
Responding on X, Hugging Face co-founder and chief science officer Thomas Wolf called the move an “Impressive level of openness on such a large run.”
However, what Xiaomi’s putting out alongside the finished models is arguably just as interesting. The company has released the model weights under the permissive MIT license, alongside its technical report and a 9-billion-parameter Qwen-based model, intended as a starting point for further agentic RL research.
“Impressive level of openness on such a large run.”
Xiaomi says it has also “fully open-sourced” a broader set of RL resources: more than 7,000 task environments spanning software engineering, vulnerability reproduction, knowledge work and web development; an end-to-end training framework covering everything from environment interaction to reward evaluation and policy optimization; and lightweight agent harnesses for experimenting with different tools, prompts and context setups. At the time of writing, however, Xiaomi’s link to the open-source collection on Hugging Face contain only the three model releases, with the 7,000-plus environments and other supporting resources not surfaced there. Luo had said earlier that Xiaomi would be open-sourcing the various elements “over the coming weeks.”
As the results began arriving this week, attention in the research community quickly moved beyond the benchmark score to what Xiaomi had committed to releasing overall. Elie Bakouch, a former Hugging Face researcher who is now a research engineer at Prime Intellect, singled out the promised RL resources.
“The most insane part, they will release ~7k RL training data and the framework leading to this top 6 model on AA,” Bakouch writes on X. “They also shipped the model + tech report less than 1 week after starting the final RL run.”
Wolf went further, arguing that access to the environments in which models learn may now be especially valuable for open research, as more model development shifts toward RL with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Because RLVR depends on tasks whose outcomes can be automatically checked — whether code passes a test, for example — the environments themselves become a crucial ingredient in training.
“Releasing many high quality open-source RL environments is the most impactful thing anyone can do to push the open-source frontier right now.”
“Releasing many high quality open-source RL environments is the most impactful thing anyone can do to push the open-source frontier right now,” Wolf writes. “The equivalent of sharing high quality pretraining data, but in the new RLVR paradigm.”
Open-weight vs open-source
So while the benchmarks around Xiaomi’s latest model are notable in their own right, it’s the company’s approach that is generating much of the fanfare so far.
Indeed, MiMo-V2.6 serves as a useful example of a distinction that often gets muddied in the AI sphere: “open-weight” and “open-source” are routinely used as though they mean the same thing, but they don’t. Many “open” models amount largely to downloadable weights — essentially, the vast collection of numerical values a model learned during training, which can then be used to run or fine-tune it — while much of what went into producing them remains closed.
Some companies have gone further in muddying those terms. Meta, for example, has often referred to its Llama models as open-source despite significant restrictions that have led open-source advocates to push back heavily on that description.
And so MiMo-V2.6 goes further than most open-source releases. Its MIT license carries none of the conditions that the likes of Moonshot’s Kimi K3 and Alibaba’s Qwen3.8-Max attach for large commercial users. And if the environments are released as promised, outside researchers will have much more of the post-training process to inspect and build on.

At Snapdragon Summit 2026, Qualcomm has announced the Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2 platform. The new platform uses Snapdragon Sound technologies and on-device AI; it is security-focused and cloud-connected, and it offers micro-power Wi-Fi 6E — which seems like a lot of technology for earbuds.

Expect lossless audio with rich sound and immersive audio quality. With Qualcomm XPAN, you’ll have more connectivity beyond regular Bluetooth range. articles.title: Microsoft brings Snapdragon X2 Plus to 13-inch Surface Laptop, 12-inch Surface Pro — low-end systems finally get upgrades
articles.text:
Microsoft brings Snapdragon X2 Plus to 13-inch Surface Laptop, 12-inch Surface Pro — low-end systems finally get upgrades
The change was announced at Qualcomm's Snapdragon Summit
Microsoft is finally updating its lowest-end computers: the 13-inch Surface Laptop and 12-inch Surface Pro. Both systems are getting the Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Plus processor (including an 80 TOPS NPU), up from a first-gen Snapdragon X Plus. The company announced the new Surfaces on its blog, in timing with Qualcomm's Snapdragon Summit.
Both new devices will launch on October 13. The Laptop will start at $1,199, while the Surface Pro will be $1,149. These are substantial increases over the previous versions, which started at $899 and $799, respectively, when they launched.
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | Microsoft Surface Laptop (13-inch) | Microsoft Surface Pro (12-inch) | 
| CPU | Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Plus (6-core) | Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Plus (6-core) | 
| GPU | Qualcomm Adreno GPU | Qualcomm Adreno GPU | 
| Memory | 16-24GB LPDDR5x RAM | 16-24GB LPDDR5x RAM | 
| Storage | 256GB, 512GB UFS | 256GB, 512GB UFS | 
| Display | 13-inch, 1920 x 1280, 3:2, 60 Hz, 500 nits maximum | 12-inch, 2196 x 1464, 3:2, up to 90 Hz (60 Hz default), 500 nits maximum, touch | 
| Release Date | October 13 | October 13 | 
| Starting Price | $1,199 | $1,149 | 
Microsoft claims that the new systems are 17% faster in Microsoft Office workloads, up to 18% more efficient on battery, offer "more than" 60% faster graphics, and have up to 95% faster AI inferencing on the NPU. Those are all compared to previous-generation Snapdragon X Plus processors.
Both systems are getting a new black color and 25% brighter displays than previous generations. The 12-inch Pro will also receive optional 5G connectivity, but only in enterprise versions of the device.
The Surface Pro will also introduce Ink Canvas, a new sketching and annotating app for Windows 11. It comes preinstalled on the new tablet and will be available for other Surface and supported Windows 11 devices through the Microsoft Store.
Surface Mouse
Beyond the two new Surface systems, the company is also announcing a new Surface Mouse. The $79.99 mouse includes haptic feedback, which has only been on some Surface notebooks so far. This can take advantage of features built into Windows 11 that allow for haptic responses for actions such as hovering over the exit button or resizing windows. Logitech's recently released MX Master 4 mouse also supports haptics.
Microsoft's pointer is designed for ambidextrous use (unlike the MX Master 4), connects over Bluetooth 6.0, uses two AAA batteries, and comes in both black and platinum colors. Like the laptops, it will launch on October 13.

articles.title: Netflix revela la velocidad de internet ideal para ver Las Guerreras K-pop en Full HD
articles.text:
Para reproducir Las Guerreras K-pop en Full HD o 1080p, la aplicación de Netflix sugiere contar con una velocidad de internet estable de al menos 5 Mb/s. Ese nivel permite acceder a una imagen con mayor definición y detalle que la calidad HD estándar de 720p, siempre que el dispositivo, el plan contratado y la red lo permitan.
La cifra es una referencia para una reproducción sin interrupciones en un solo dispositivo. En un hogar donde otros dispositivos descargan archivos, realizan videollamadas, actualizan aplicaciones o usan plataformas de video, puede ser necesario disponer de más capacidad para conservar la resolución durante toda la película.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué velocidad se necesita para ver la película en HD y 4K
Netflix establece una diferencia entre las dos resoluciones. Para ver contenido en HD de 720p, la plataforma sugiere una conexión de 3 Mb/s o más. Esa velocidad puede ser suficiente en una red con poco uso y un solo dispositivo conectado a la reproducción.
El salto a 4K requiere al menos 15 Mb/s. Esta resolución ofrece una imagen más definida, con mayor cantidad de píxeles en pantalla. La disponibilidad depende de las características del televisor, la computadora, el teléfono o la tableta desde donde se acceda al catálogo.
Por qué la velocidad contratada puede no llegar al dispositivo principal
La velocidad informada en un plan de internet no siempre coincide con el rendimiento que recibe el dispositivo donde se reproduce la película. La distancia entre el dispositivo y el router, las paredes, los muebles y otros obstáculos pueden reducir la intensidad de la señal WiFi.
PUBLICIDAD
Además, influyen la cantidad de aparatos conectados y las tareas activas en la red. Una computadora que descarga una actualización, un teléfono que respalda archivos en la nube o una consola conectada a internet pueden restar capacidad disponible.
Qué sucede si la conexión pierde estabilidad durante la reproducción
La plataforma streaming ajusta de forma automática la calidad de imagen según las condiciones de la red. Si detecta que la conexión pierde velocidad o presenta variaciones, puede reducir la resolución de manera temporal para evitar que el video se detenga.
Una imagen borrosa al comienzo de Las Guerreras K-pop o durante una escena puede responder a ese mecanismo de adaptación. Si el servicio identifica una mejora en la conexión, vuelve a elevar la calidad disponible. La continuidad del contenido suele tener prioridad frente a la máxima resolución posible.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo se puede comprobar si hay suficiente conexión a internet
La comprobación más útil consiste en realizar una prueba de velocidad desde el mismo dispositivo que se utilizará para reproducir Netflix. El resultado debe alcanzar, como mínimo, los 3 Mb/s para HD o los 5 Mb/s para Full HD, aunque conviene que la medición sea superior si la red se comparte con otras personas.
Asimismo, la estabilidad importa tanto como el número final de la prueba. Una conexión que registra picos altos, pero cae de forma frecuente, genera pausas o cambios de calidad. Si el resultado queda por debajo, es preferible revisar la señal antes de iniciar la película.
Qué cambios ayudan a mejorar la reproducción de la película en casa
La ubicación del router puede modificar la experiencia de visualización. Conviene colocarlo en una zona central y elevada, lejos de muebles cerrados, objetos metálicos y otros aparatos electrónicos que puedan afectar la cobertura. Acercar el televisor, la computadora o la tableta al router mejora la señal.
PUBLICIDAD
Los dispositivos pueden conectarse a la red WiFi de 5 GHz, que suele ofrecer mayor velocidad a corta distancia que la banda de 2,4 GHz. Para una pantalla principal, la conexión mediante cable Ethernet reduce interferencias y aporta mayor estabilidad.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: OpenAI lance GPT-6 Sol et Luna : deux nouveaux modèles IA dévoilés en réponse à la concurrence
articles.text:
OpenAI a lancé deux nouveaux modèles, qui se veulent aussi efficaces qu’abordables. Leurs noms ? GPT-6 Sol et GPT-6 Luna.
Impossible de s’ennuyer chez OpenAI. Ayant renoncé à faire son entrée en Bourse cette année, la firme a dû geler les inscriptions à son forfait Pro, face au succès retentissant de son modèle GPT-6 Astra. Souhaitant malgré tout étendre ses sources de revenus, elle a créé ce mois-ci des offres pour les géants de la finance. Elle vient également de dévoiler deux nouveaux modèles. Découvrons-les ensemble.
OpenAI lance deux nouveaux modèles, Sol et Luna
Les deux technologies permettront aux utilisateurs de faire de précieuses économies sans dire adieu aux performances. En effet, avec Sol et Luna, les tarifs diminuent de moitié : il faudra compter 2 dollars pour un million de tokens en entrée et 10 dollars en sortie pour le premier contre 0,10 dollar en entrée et 0,50 dollar en sortie pour le second. Les développeurs apprécieront, même si l’annonce compare ces prix avec les tarifs promotionnels de la génération 5.6.
Des modèles plus fiables et moins bavards
OpenAI a entraîné Sol et Luna avec des méthodes proches de celles utilisées pour Astra et, sans surprise, les deux modèles ont le même style de réponse que leur grand frère. Exit donc le jargon à outrance et les détails superflus.
Avec ces nouveaux modèles, la firme souhaite aussi faire la chasse aux erreurs : « GPT-6 Sol commet environ deux fois moins d'erreurs que son prédécesseur, offrant une fiabilité proche de celle d'Astra à un coût bien moindre. GPT-6 Luna affiche également des progrès considérables ; à des niveaux d'effort plus élevés, il égale GPT-5.6 Sol pour un coût environ cent fois inférieur », affirme OpenAI dans son annonce. Ces résultats reposent toutefois sur des tests maison.
Concernant les évaluations externes, la firme a surtout son concurrent Anthropic dans le viseur : pour le code, on peut lire que « GPT-6 Sol (…) parvient à égaler les résultats de Claude Fable 5.1 en mode « xhigh » à un coût bien moindre » et pour l’utilisation sur ordinateur, que « GPT-6 Sol à (…) obtient un score similaire à celui de Claude Opus 5 à un niveau d’effort « medium » — 60,5 % contre 60,3 % — pour un coût par tâche inférieur d’environ 80 %. » Hélas, Anthropic ayant dégainé Opus 5.5 à peine une heure et demie avant cette annonce, ces comparaisons sont d’ores et déjà datées.
- Chat dans différentes langues, dont le français
- Générer, traduire et obtenir un résumé de texte
- Générer, optimiser et corriger du code
Sol et Luna seront disponibles dans ChatGPT Work et Codex pour les abonnés Plus, pro, Business, Enterprise et Edu. Les comptes Free et Go pourront accéder à Luna via leur application de bureau. Malheureusement, le grand public devra prendre son mal en patience : il est, pour l'instant, impossible de tester les nouveaux modèles sur le chat en ligne.

articles.title: Q-Day: Der gefürchtete Tag, an dem Quantencomputer unsere Verschlüsselung knacken, rückt näher
articles.text:
Post-quantum Kryptographie: So sollen unsere Daten selbst in der Quantencomputern-Ära sicher sein
Verschlüsselung klingt nach Geheimnis, Spionage oder Dissidenz. Dabei ist sie überall: Beim Online-Banking, wenn wir Nachrichten per Chat austauschen, bei jedem Online-Bestellvorgang wird der Datenaustausch verschlüsselt. Und jeder Patch, jedes Update wird kryptografisch signiert. Unser Vertrauen in die Sicherheit all dieser Vorgänge gründet auf Einwegfunktionen – Berechnungen, die in einer Richtung einfach auszuführen, in der anderen aber extrem aufwendig zu berechnen sind – selbst mit extrem leistungsstarken Computern. Hinreichend leistungsfähige Quantencomputer würden diesen Mechanismus aushebeln und herkömmliche Verschlüsselungen innerhalb von Stunden knacken.
Dieser Text erscheint in der Ausgabe 7/2026 von MIT Technology Review. Darin beschäftigen wir uns damit, wie KI die IT-Sicherheit auf den Kopf stellt. Das Heft erscheint am 25.9.2026 im Zeitschriftenhandel.
Der Tag, an dem solch ein Computer zum ersten Mal online geht, hat einen Namen: Sicherheitsfachleute nennen ihn den Q-Day. Und sie gehen davon aus, dass böswillige Akteure bereits jetzt verschlüsselt übertragene Daten abspeichern, um sie irgendwann später mit einem Quantencomputer zu knacken. Post-quantum Cryptography (PQC) soll mathematische Methoden verwenden, die auch mächtige Quantencomputer nicht brechen können.

articles.title: Francia está descubriendo que el más mínimo desequilibrio le deja sin diésel. España tiene una forma de evitarlo
articles.text:
Francia tiene problemas de abastecimiento de gasolina. Desde el estallido de la guerra en Irán y los ataques de Ucrania a las refinerías rusas, el suministro mundial de combustible está en una situación crítica. Algo que no ha hecho más que agravarse en los últimos tiempos con los ataques hutíes a las infraestructuras sauditas y que podría ir a más de confirmarse los deseos de Donald Trump de cerrar el grifo de sus propias exportaciones.
Pero no solo es el propio suministro lo que importa. Todo esto pilla a Europa cerrando refinerías, un negocio hasta ahora algo ruinoso y poco alineado con los objetivos de cero emisiones netas que se habían propuesto en el continente, como explican desde Oil Price. Y aquí es precisamente donde España se guarda un as en la manga: nuestro país cuenta con ocho refinerías operativas que hacen que el impacto sea algo menor.
Situación crítica, en cifras. Nuestro país vecino está sufriendo de forma notable las consecuencias de la geopolítica internacional en sus estaciones de servicio. Según la web oficial del gobierno, el 11% de las estaciones de servicio presenta problemas de abastecimiento a día de hoy, aunque se ha llegado a alcanzar el 15%. La mayoría de estas estaciones se encuentran en París y alrededores, donde la mitad de las gasolineras ya no tienen ningún tipo de combustible, informa laSexta.
En el mes de septiembre, según este medio, Francia demandó 750 mil barriles de gasóleo, cuando su producción nacional apenas alcanzaba los 370 mil. Es decir, hasta ahora importaban la mitad de su demanda. Cuando esta demanda ha empezado a sufrir los embates de una situación internacional cada vez más volátil, con las dificultades de transporte del crudo, el desabastecimiento ha empezado a ser una realidad.
¿A qué se debe esta escasez? Los ataques de las fuerzas iraníes contra los oleoductos y la costa de Arabia Saudí han comprometido el suministro de petróleo de Europa y han disparado los precios en las últimas semanas hasta alcanzar su nivel más alto desde febrero de este año. Además, la ofensiva contra las refinerías rusas por parte de Ucrania y la prórroga de Putin sobre la prohibición de exportar diésel hasta octubre, como apunta Oil Price, también han contribuido a la pérdida de barriles que hoy está sufriendo Francia.
Cuenta The Telegraph que todo este cóctel ha desatado una oleada de compras de pánico que se han extendido por todo el país que ha dejado a una gran parte de las gasolineras francesas sin, al menos, un tipo de combustible. De hecho, las estaciones de servicio de TotalEnergies, las únicas que han fijado precios máximos (2,25 euros el litro de diésel y 1,99 euros el de gasolina) son las que antes se han agotado y las que más están sufriendo las consecuencias de este desabastecimiento.
Macron ya ha pedido relajar medidas. Ante esta crisis petrolera, el presidente francés Emmanuel Macron ha escrito una carta a Bruselas pidiendo que se pongan en marcha mecanismos de emergencia para afrontar la crisis. De manera interna, el ejecutivo francés ha extendido ayudas a los consumidores, con una partida de más de 1.400 millones de euros que llega en plena lucha por controlar su gasto público.
En la misiva del 18 de septiembre, el mandatario instaba a la presidenta de la Comisión Europea Ursula von der Leyen a maximizar la producción de combustible y la capacidad de refinación de nuestro continente. Para ello, habría que flexibilizar parte de la norma que especifica las características de los combustibles como la densidad, la volatilidad y la desulfuración, y, en definitiva, fabricar carburante de peor calidad. Macron también solicita el aplazamiento de las nuevas normas europeas sobre las emisiones de metano.
Cuando las barbas de tu vecino veas cortar… o no. España, al igual que el resto de Europa, afronta el mismo escenario que describe Macron, pero con un as en la manga. Al contrario que en otros países, entre 2008 y 2011 las compañías de petróleo españolas apostaron fuerte por el sector y hoy nuestro país cuenta con ocho refinerías de gran capacidad: cinco plantas son de Repsol (Cartagena, Tarragona, Bilbao, Puertollano y A Coruña), dos de Moeve (Huelva y Algeciras) y una de BP (Castellón). En total, su producción es del 13% del total europeo, solo superada por la de Alemania y la de Italia.
Frente a las cifras ya vistas del país vecino en septiembre, España necesitó 600 mil barriles de crudo, de los cuales produjo internamente 500 mil. Gracias a esto, cabría pensar que estamos mejor preparados que Francia, que depende más de importaciones de diésel y está más expuesta.
Refinerías a pleno rendimiento. La ventaja de España no se queda solo en la capacidad de refinamiento, sino también en la diversidad de crudos que pueden tratar las plantas españolas: según cifras de Bankinter, en España se reciben 30 variedades distintas de petróleo procedentes de 20 países y hoy están trabajando más que nunca. Tanto es así que Inés Cardenal, portavoz de la patronal petrolera AICE, ha comentado en declaraciones a la Cadena SER que «España es el país mejor preparado en este momento para abordar lo que la Agencia Internacional de la Energía ha calificado como 'la peor crisis de suministro de la historia'».
¿Significa que España está a salvo de todo? Sin embargo, esto no significa que seamos inmunes o que España pueda aislarse de una crisis mundial. Como explica Macron en su carta, una crisis de carburantes, es, al final, una crisis subyacente de la oferta, ya que cuando sube el diésel, sube todo lo demás, especialmente algo tan diario y necesario como la cesta de la compra. Y de eso es más difícil librarse.
Imagen | Tom Fisk
