articles.title: Meta’s AI agent is a cute little guy who’s great at spending my money
articles.text:
Modern life comes with an unending, auto-populating to-do list.
Meta’s AI agent is a cute little guy who’s great at spending my money
Muse did a decent job with my to-do list, but boy is it handy with a credit card.
Meta’s AI agent is a cute little guy who’s great at spending my money
Muse did a decent job with my to-do list, but boy is it handy with a credit card.
It never ceases to amaze me how I can be doing nothing at all, minding my own business, and suddenly something needs to be taken care of. You’re telling me a tree branch fell in the backyard and now I have to figure out what to do with it? The tree just assigned me homework? Oh, our trash collection company canceled our account out of nowhere and now I have to send email about it? Repeatedly? Totally unfair.
These are the things that we’ve been told for years that AI will help us with. We’ll all have a smart virtual assistant to triage and handle the tedious tasks we’d rather not face. If you believe Meta, that future is available right now in the form of Muse, its AI agent for the masses. I put it to the test doing exactly what it’s advertised to do: taking care of tedious crap I’ve been putting off for ages. And it worked better than I expected — especially when there was a credit card transaction to be made.
It was dizzying watching Marley spin up virtual browser windows chasing down my requests
Marley — one of the suggested names you can give Muse’s avatar — had been pinging me all of last week. It wanted me to know all the ways it could be useful; I was too busy to engage with it. But I sat down with it this week and set it to work on a task. And while it worked on that task, I gave it another. Then another. The thing about AI agents is that they’re most useful when you use them in parallel with each other. Or that’s the theory I was working on. In reality, it was dizzying watching Marley spin up virtual browser windows chasing down my requests. I went with a generically cute snowman-meets-puppy avatar that Meta suggested at setup, and Marley tapped cheerfully on a keyboard as it worked its way through my commands.
In the span of a morning, I gave it the following tasks to help me out with. None of them were critical; mostly they were the kinds of pebble-in-your-shoe annoyances I’d put off for weeks, months, or maybe years. Here’s how it went.
Task: Follow up with the landscaper working on a bid for our backyard renovation
Effort rating: Extremely low
Time I have been putting it off: Two weeks
Was Marley able to complete it? Yes
I asked Marley to help me nudge the person I’ve been emailing at a local landscaping company. I’m expecting them to price out some yard renovations for us, so Marley requested access to my Gmail to check on the status of that project. It confirmed that more time had passed than the landscaper initially estimated the bid would take, and drafted a rather snippy but wordy email. “Make it shorter,” I said. To be clear: As a rule, I do not use AI writing tools. Definitely not in my work, and not even for email. What’s the point? Just don’t send email if you’re going to have a robot write it. In fact, I think we should abolish email. Anyway, I broke my own rule for testing purposes; hitting send on that message made me cringe.
Task: Buy a replacement steam wand assembly for my espresso machine
Effort rating: Low
Time I have been putting it off: [redacted] years
Was Marley able to complete it? Mostly
My Breville Barista Express has held up spectacularly for six years and counting, but it isn’t immune from user error. I took the steam wand apart to clean it a few years back and tore the little silicone washer that goes inside of it. Instead of ordering a new one, I just shoved it back into place and screwed the thing back together. It works okay, but every few months when I’m cleaning the machine it nags at my conscience. It’s probably why the hot water dispenser drips sometimes when I run the steam, too. Ordering a new steam wand assembly costs like 7 bucks and is as difficult as entering my credit card number on Breville’s website. Naturally, I put it off for an unreasonable amount of time.
I opened up my chat with Marley and told it what I needed; it found the part and added it to a shopping cart. I had to finish up the order myself, but it’s done and the part will be here in five to seven business days.
Task: Downgrade my security system account to the cheaper one
Effort rating: Medium (requires a phone call)
Time I have been putting it off: A year? Two years???
Was Marley able to complete it? Not fully
I approved Marley to log into my account, which also required me to verify my email. While I was making the trip to my inbox I saw I had a follow-up to my follow-up with the landscaper. He was apologetic for the delay and I felt a little bad about the slightly abrupt tone of the email Marley sent. I wrote a friendlier reply the old-fashioned way.
With access to my account, Marley reported back what I already knew: You have to call the company to change your plan. Muse wasn’t able to make a phone call for me, though apparently that ability is in the works. This seems like the logical next frontier for these AI agents, and also a weird future to consider. I call the company and answer a few questions from their robot before I’m routed to a human. No doubt there’s a future soon where Marley talks to the security company’s robot before any human being enters the chat. Or more likely in the short term, a human in a call center talks to the other company’s robot before eventually getting to another human in a call center, which feels even weirder. But surely the end state is that my robot will just talk to their robot and they’ll do business without any intervention at all. Anyway, a nice guy answered and made the change to my account. I think he was real.
Task: Contact a junk removal company to get rid of a fallen tree branch in the backyard
Effort rating: Medium
Time I have been putting it off: A week
Was Marley able to complete it? Mostly
The tree branch is a real problem I need to deal with. It didn’t do any damage, but it’s big enough that it’ll either take an afternoon to hack apart and haul to the dump or requires a visit from a junk removal service. Marley was most useful here — it set off looking through listings for hauling services and highlighted a few in the area. It asked for my address, phone number, and a photo of the tree limb, and used that information to put together requests for quotes from a couple of companies using online form submissions. I got a text back from one company not long after, and confirmed a time the following day for tree limb removal. Very little was required on my part, and assuming the tree branch is gone by this time tomorrow, I’ll consider this mission accomplished for Muse.
Task: Shop for camping kitchen gear, either as a set or assembled piece by piece
Effort rating: Medium
Time I have been putting it off: A few days
Was Marley able to complete it? Yes
If our wallets were already defenseless in the era of one-click checkout, we’re so cooked when AI agent shopping truly arrives. I gave Marley some requirements for my outdoor cooking setup and it set out finding the necessary items. It made an attempt to access Amazon and was roundly blocked, complete with a spicy message about AI agents violating terms of service. Anyway, it found what I was looking for between OXO’s own website and Walmart.
While I was at it, I wanted to add a propane fire pit to the mix. Not for cooking — for ambience and marshmallows. I’d borrowed a couple of different kinds from friends, and after weighing the pros and cons of each with Muse I landed on a LavaBox and a handy carrying case. The grand total for my camp kitchen and burn-ban-safe fire pit: $500! I told Muse we’d have to pump the brakes and spread these purchases out over the winter. It obliged and helped me prioritize what would make sense to buy first and what was likely to go on sale toward the holidays.
In the meantime, I had Marley find and purchase some other espresso machine supplies. I had to connect my credit card via Stripe, but after I’d done that once it became dangerously easy to tell Marley “Go for it” and approve whatever it had just put in my shopping cart. I watched it fill in my address details in the virtual browser window and confirmation emails started filing into my inbox. Marley did a little shopping around to find slightly better prices, and I didn’t buy anything egregious — just some descaling powder and water filters. It also did the math to calculate whether powdered Dezcal would be a better value than the liquid stuff (way better, not surprisingly). But it is shockingly easy to spend money when a cute little guy is running around the internet with your credit card.
It is shockingly easy to spend money when a cute little guy is running around the internet with your credit card
There’s a danger in overcommitting yourself when you feel like these AI tools are speeding you up. In a few cases, Muse helped me get started by putting the details I needed in front of my face. I had the phone number for the home security company at hand, as well as the name of my current plan and the one I wanted to downgrade to. Getting that little speed bump out of the way was what I needed, I guess. But the dirty secret of productivity hacks is that doing more stuff often doesn’t feel like things are being removed from your plate; somehow it just invites more tasks.
If you’re willing to give a lot of information and trust to Meta — a massive caveat! — Muse can genuinely help you get things done. I’d been using it for all of 40 minutes and already given it my full name, address, credit card number, a photo of my backyard, and the credentials for my home security account login. Going great, I’d say! If AI decides to kill us all I just secured my spot at the front of the line. Meta of course says that all of these details are stored securely, Marley allegedly can’t even see them, etc., but still. Unsettling.
But I think the underlying question we need to ask ourselves as we enter the era of AI agents is what we do with the time we’re supposedly freeing up. Will we use it to take on more commitments? And then ultimately feel overwhelmed again when the to-do list keeps piling up? After a morning crossing items off my list with Marley, I didn’t spend the hours that followed doing anything consequential. In fact, I spent that time chatting with Marley, seeking reassurance about the direction of the yard project and brainstorming fall camping trips I probably won’t take. It’s a gorgeous day outside, the kind we really can’t take for granted in late September, and I wish I’d spent that time outdoors rather than inside talking to a robot, cute little guy or otherwise.

                        Systems & Design
                        
       			
					
WHITEPAPERS
		
Functional verification is no longer only about closing the design. It is increasingly about understanding the system before silicon becomes the first place where all interactions are fully revealed.
								September 23rd, 2026 - 
								By: Siemens EDA
								
							
						
The forthcoming 2026 Siemens EDA and Wilson Research Group Functional Verification Study indicates that the IC verification problem is changing in nature, not simply growing in complexity. Declining first-silicon success, increased CPU/GPU/AI accelerator-class participation, near-universal reported embedded processor content across implementation categories, a broadening verification ecosystem, and greater visibility of firmware-, safety-, and security-related respin contributors all point toward a shift from verifying designs to building system confidence in software-driven silicon systems.

articles.title: La alternativa a las copias de seguridad en WhatsApp: mueve chats usando un código QR
articles.text:
Cambiar de teléfono ya no obliga a depender de una copia de seguridad en la nube para conservar el historial de conversaciones. WhatsApp incorporó una función de transferencia directa mediante un código QR que permite mover chats, fotografías, videos, documentos y otros archivos entre dos dispositivos sin recurrir a Google Drive ni a iCloud.
Cómo funciona la transferencia directa entre dispositivos
La herramienta reemplaza el esquema tradicional de subir la información a un servicio en la nube para luego descargarla en el nuevo equipo. En su lugar, WhatsApp establece una conexión directa entre ambos teléfonos, siempre que se mantengan cerca y tengan la aplicación instalada.
PUBLICIDAD
Cuando el usuario inicia el proceso, el dispositivo nuevo genera un código QR que debe escanearse desde el teléfono anterior. Tras ese paso, la transferencia arranca de forma automática y continúa hasta copiar toda la información disponible. El traslado incluye conversaciones, archivos multimedia, notas de voz y documentos, y conserva la estructura original de los chats.
Los pasos para completar la migración
Ambos dispositivos deben tener instalada la versión más reciente de la aplicación antes de comenzar. En el teléfono antiguo, el usuario debe abrir WhatsApp y seguir esta ruta: ingresar a Ajustes, seleccionar Chats y pulsar Transferir chats.
En el teléfono nuevo aparecerá entonces un código QR, que debe escanearse con el dispositivo anterior para iniciar el proceso. Es necesario mantener la aplicación abierta en los dos equipos hasta que la transferencia finalice por completo, ya que interrumpirla antes de tiempo podría provocar que parte de la información no llegue al dispositivo de destino.
PUBLICIDAD
La copia de seguridad tradicional continúa disponible
Pese a que el nuevo sistema evita depender de internet para subir archivos a la nube, WhatsApp mantiene el mecanismo clásico de copias de seguridad. En Android, estas se almacenan en Google Drive, mientras que en iPhone utilizan iCloud.
Para generar una copia de seguridad, el usuario debe acceder a Ajustes, ingresar en Chats, seleccionar Copia de seguridad y pulsar Guardar después de vincular la cuenta de almacenamiento correspondiente. Esta vía sigue resultando útil cuando el teléfono anterior ya no está disponible o cuando los dos dispositivos no pueden permanecer juntos durante la migración.
Recomendaciones previas al cambio de equipo
Antes de iniciar cualquier transferencia conviene verificar que el nuevo dispositivo cuente con espacio de almacenamiento suficiente para recibir todos los archivos. También se aconseja conectar ambos teléfonos a una red WiFi estable, dado que una interrupción de la conexión puede retrasar o afectar el proceso.
PUBLICIDAD
Otra precaución consiste en revisar la fecha de la última copia de seguridad, con el fin de confirmar que incluya las conversaciones más recientes. Los especialistas recomiendan además no desinstalar WhatsApp ni restaurar el teléfono antiguo a su configuración de fábrica hasta comprobar que todos los chats y archivos se transfirieron correctamente.
Las limitaciones al cambiar entre sistemas operativos distintos
La transferencia mediante código QR está diseñada para dispositivos que comparten el mismo sistema operativo, es decir, funciona entre dos teléfonos Android o entre dos iPhone. Cuando el cambio se realiza entre plataformas diferentes, como de Android a iOS o viceversa, WhatsApp requiere un procedimiento distinto que suele apoyarse en herramientas adicionales.
PUBLICIDAD
En el caso de los dispositivos de Apple, la compañía ofrece la aplicación Trasladar a iOS, que permite mover parte de la información desde un teléfono Android durante la configuración inicial del nuevo equipo.
El cifrado se mantiene durante todo el proceso
Uno de los aspectos centrales del sistema es que la transferencia conserva el cifrado de extremo a extremo característico de WhatsApp. Esto implica que los mensajes, fotografías, videos y demás archivos permanecen protegidos durante toda la migración y solo pueden ser leídos por los dispositivos involucrados en el proceso.
La función busca simplificar el cambio de teléfono para quienes desean conservar intacto su historial de conversaciones sin depender exclusivamente de las copias de seguridad en la nube.

articles.title: Qualcomm dévoile les Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 : les puces 2 nm des futurs smartphones Android
articles.text:
Chaque automne, Qualcomm donne le tempo des smartphones Android de l’année à venir. Le cru dévoilé le 22 septembre réserve une surprise de structure : le haut de gamme se scinde en deux, entre un Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 « classique » et une déclinaison Elite Extreme Gen 6 réservée aux appareils les plus ambitieux. Les deux étrennent une gravure en 2 nanomètres, à l’instar d’Apple et Mediatek, ainsi que des fréquences jamais vues sur téléphone.
5 GHz et 2 nanomètres : la course aux records continue
Les deux puces alignent deux cœurs Prime poussés jusqu’à 5,0 GHz et six cœurs Performance à 4,0 GHz, une première pour un processeur mobile. Face à la génération précédente, le modèle standard promet 10 % de puissance en plus côté processeur, 35 % côté graphismes et 14 % sur la partie IA. L’Extreme monte d’un cran, avec des gains respectifs de 13 %, 44 % et 35 %, et s’arroge quelques exclusivités. Au menu : moitié de mémoire partagée en plus, 18 Mo dédiés au circuit graphique et la vidéo 8K à 60 images par seconde. Le modèle standard plafonne, lui, à 30 images par seconde dans cette définition. Qualcomm promet même, pour cette version Extreme, l’exécution locale de modèles d’IA dépassant les 30 milliards de paramètres, une affirmation à vérifier une fois les téléphones en main.
Les premiers appareils ne traîneront pas : Motorola a déjà officialisé son Signature 27 sous Elite Extreme Gen 6 pour la fin d’année. OnePlus et iQOO suivront avec leurs prochains fleurons, et Xiaomi ferait partie des tout premiers servis.
Deux puces haut de gamme pour amortir la flambée des prix
Cette scission intervient dans un contexte tarifaire sous tension. Qualcomm a confirmé fin juillet une hausse de ses tarifs, à deux chiffres selon les courriers adressés à ses clients cet été, effective sur les puces livrées depuis le 1er septembre. L’entreprise invoque une « hausse généralisée des coûts » touchant la fabrication, l’assemblage, les tests et la mémoire. Les estimations qui circulent situent la galette de silicium gravée en 2 nanomètres autour de 30 000 dollars pièce, pendant que la crise de la mémoire vive alourdit déjà la facture de chaque smartphone. Le composant le plus prestigieux du téléphone Android renchérit donc au moment précis où tout le reste augmente aussi.
Vu le contexte, proposer deux étages de haut de gamme fait office de soupape. Les constructeurs soucieux de contenir leurs tarifs peuvent s’en tenir au Snapdragon « standard », déjà largement suffisant pour l’immense majorité des usages, et réserver l’Extreme aux modèles vendus au sommet de la gamme, dont les acheteurs ne regardent plus l’étiquette depuis longtemps. Qualcomm préfère parler d’« un choix plus large » offert aux marques ; on peut aussi y lire une tentative de garder des prix à peu près cohérents, en cantonnant les surcoûts les plus spectaculaires aux téléphones capables de les absorber. Le premier Motorola Signature, lancé à 999 euros en février, donne d’ailleurs une idée du ticket d’entrée de cette catégorie.

articles.title: The Nothing Phone (4a) Pro hits its lowest price yet — here's why one of our favorite mid-range phones is a great alternative to Apple and Samsung
articles.text:
The Nothing Phone (4a) Pro hits its lowest price yet — here's why this exceptional device is a great alternative to Apple and Samsung
This 2026 mid-range phone is absolutely worth checking out
Headlines at this time of year are usually dominated by iPhones — and you'd expect nothing less, considering Apple always unveils its next-gen devices in September. Nonetheless, Android fans aren't being completely left in the dark.

In terms of sheer bang for the buck, there's definitely a strong argument for the Nothing Phone (4a) Pro — especially if you want to break away from the usual suspects.
Even though we're on the cusp of another Amazon Prime Day (there's another sale in two weeks), I'd say this one is well worth a look. Today's best phone deal at Amazon
Looking for something a little different? Amazon currently has the excellent Nothing Phone (4a) Pro listed at its lowest price yet. A worthy alternative to the big names?
The Nothing Phone (4a) Pro is positioned as a mid-range phone that tries to deliver flagship-style features without the high price.
Its biggest strengths are its distinctive design, huge 6.83-inch 144Hz AMOLED display, clean Android 16 software, Glyph Matrix notification system, and surprisingly strong gaming performance from the Snapdragon 7 Gen 4. articles.title: Meta's new transoceanic undersea cable boasts a whopping petabit of bandwidth — Petal link between US and France will be twice as fast as the last
articles.text:
Meta's new transoceanic undersea cable boasts a whopping petabit of bandwidth — Petal link between US and France will be twice as fast as the last
Petal puts the mere 500 terabits of Meta's old Anjana cable to shame
Meta has announced plans to build and install a new subsea cable that will connect France and the United States at a breakneck 1 Pbps (1 petabit per second or 1,000 terabits per second). It will become the most advanced subsea cable at its length and blow Meta's own 0.5 Pbps Anjana cable system out of the water. Figuratively, of course.
Anjana runs from Spain to the US for a total distance of 4,425 miles at a relatively leisurely 480 Tbps thanks to its 24 fiber pairs. But Petal ratchets things up a notch, using 48 fiber pairs and a two-core fiber-based solution (with 24 pairs each) to achieve 1 Pbps across transatlantic distances.
Meta claims that the new cable will have enough network capacity to allow 75% of the planet's population to stream music at the same time — so long as they stick to 160 kbps MP3s or lower, that is. No lossless streaming for you.
Either way, you'll have to wait a while for your theoretical music fix. Meta says that Petal is expected to enter service in 2029. It'll be built in partnership with NEC and Sumitomo Electric Industries, with support for the French landing from Orange.
Subsea cables might not be at the top of many internet users' minds, but they're vital to the way our connected world functions today — and they've often been the subject of sabotage plots as a result. As the number of connected devices continues to grow, these cables become all the more important. And they need to be fast and reliable.
Meta says that its decision to use a two-core fiber design for Petal brought complications along with its huge performance. Minimizing crosstalk is key, as is ensuring low attenuation throughout the length of the cable.
The fix for the attenuation involves using ultra-pure synthetic silica during the manufacture of the preform, while crosstalk is minimized by "carefully controlling for high refractive indexes in the cores against lower indexes within the surrounding medium and counter-propagating the optical signals."
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Meta says that a subsea cable of this length typically needs around 100 repeaters to get the signal from one end to the other without degradation. Petal uses single-body 96-amp repeaters, each with single-core fiber amplification and a Fan-In/Fan-Out (FIFO) interface to convert two-core fiber into two single-core fibers inside the repeater before converting it back to two-core fiber following amplification. The theory is that this approach will allow Petal to retain the efficiency and reliability afforded by single-core amplification.
As for why Meta feels the need to build such a cable, it points to its desire to bring "greater capacity, stronger resiliency, and future-proof infrastructure to Europe as demand for communications and reliable connectivity continues to increase." We hope that dual-core fiber isn't twice as tasty to the average shark.

Oliver Haslam has written about technology of all shapes and sizes for over 15 years, both online and in print. He's fascinated by how personal computing continues to change as tower PCs give way to foldable phones and beyond.

articles.title: Nissan dévoile la PIXO, sa citadine électrique à moins de 20 000 euros basée sur la Twingo
articles.text:
Chose promise, chose due. Nissan avait annoncé une petite citadine électrique à moins de 20 000 € bâtie sur la Renault Twingo, la voici présentée officiellement ce 23 septembre 2026. Fabriquée par Renault dans l’usine slovène de Novo Mesto, la nouvelle Pixo partage sa plateforme avec la Twingo E-Tech (et la nouvelle Dacia Spring).
Nissan complète ainsi sa gamme de « cousins » électriques, après les lancements de la Micra, basée sur la R5, et la Leaf, reprenant la plateforme du Scénic. Grâce à Renault, le constructeur japonais fait son grand retour sur le segment des petites citadines. Une manière d’aller plus vite, imitant la rapidité des marques chinoises pour survivre.
Sous la carrosserie de la Pixo, une Twingo
Techniquement, la Pixo et la Twingo sont strictement identiques. Même batterie LFP de 27,5 kWh, même moteur de 82 ch et même temps de recharge rapide qui fait passer la batterie de 15 à 80 % en 28 minutes. L’autonomie annoncée ? 259 km WLTP, soit 4 km de moins que la Twingo. Autant dire rien.
Contrairement à la Dacia Spring, la Nissan Pixo reprend le système d’info-divertissement comprenant les services Google. La petite citadine japonaise hérite également de la modularité de la Française avec les deux sièges arrière coulissants, qui permettent de jongler entre un volume de coffre de 260 et 356 litres.
La recharge rapide livrée de série sur la Nissan Pixo
La belle surprise sur cette Pixo est sur la recharge rapide. Celle-ci est fournie de série sur toute la gamme, alors qu’elle se paie en option 500 € sur la Twingo, même dans sa version la plus haute. Reste à voir si la Pixo offrira le mode One Pedal de série aussi.
Il faut bien ça pour se démarquer, car niveau prix, Nissan devrait logiquement proposer un ticket d’entrée à moins de 20 000 euros. D’autant que le style ne la distingue pas vraiment de la Twingo. articles.title: Von neuen Airpods überflüssig gemacht? Apple legt KI-Gadget auf Eis.
articles.text:
KI-Gadget von Apple soll aufs Abstellgleis geraten: Was dazu bekannt ist
Apple legt laut einem Bericht US-Wirtschaftsmagazin Bloomberg die Entwicklung eines KI-Wearable auf Eis. Es handelt sich demnach um einen tragbaren Pin, über den das Portal The Information zuerst im Januar dieses Jahres berichtet hatte.
Wearable von der Größe eines Airtag
Nutzer:innen sollten sich das Gadget, das aus Glas und Aluminium bestehen sollte, entweder an die Kleidung pinnen oder um den Hals hängen können.
Der Durchmesser des Gadgets sollten dem des Airtag entsprechen, aber etwas dicker sein als dieser. Apples 2021 vorgestellter Tracker, mit dem man die Geldbörse oder die Autoschlüssel wiederfinden kann, ist etwa so groß wie eine Zwei-Euro-Münze.
Das sollte der eingestampfte KI-Pin von Apple leisten
In dem Pin waren laut den Plänen von Apple zwei Kameras integriert, ein Standardlinse und ein Weitwinkelobjektiv. Drei Mikrofone sollten Umgebungsgeräusche einfangen.
Die Kameras und die Mikros sollten Informationen über die Umgebung der User:innen an Siri und die KI-Bilderkennung Visual Intelligence weiterleiten. Die Nutzer:innen könnten dann Fragen zu ihrer Umwelt stellen, die Siri über die am Pinn eingebauten Lautsprecher beantwortet. Das Ganze sollte völlig freihändig funktionieren.
Machen neue Airpods den KI-Anhänger überflüssig?
Hauseigene Konkurrenz könnte den eingestampften KI-Pin überflüssig gemacht haben. So sollen die geplanten neuen Airpods von Apple ebenfalls Kameras enthalten, über die sich Nutzer:innen über ihre Umgebung informieren können.
Außerdem sollen laut Bloomberg auch smarte Brillen intern Vorfahrt haben. Ein eigenes Gerät um den Hals hängen oder an den Kragen zu pinnen wäre damit nicht mehr nötig.
Apple konzentriert sich auf Fitnessband
Laut Bloomberg verlagert Apple seinen Fokus von dem Pin weg auf andere Wearables. Hauptsächlich soll es sich dabei um ein Fitnessband ohne Display handeln.
Damit macht Apple etwa dem Armband von Whoop Konkurrenz, das seinen Nutzer:innen Fitnessdaten direkt auf eine Smartphone-App schickt. User:innen der Apple Watch tragen stattdessen ein im Verhältnis zu Whoop klobiges Display am Handgelenk, das viel Akkuleistung frisst. Wie beim Whoop soll es sich beim Apple-Fitnesstracker um ein Stoffband mit Sensor handeln.

articles.title: Anthropic made Opus 5.5 cheaper. Then it broke four things your agent depends on.
articles.text:
Anthropic made Opus 5.5 cheaper. Then it broke four things your agent depends on.
Anthropic made Claude Opus 5.5, released on Tuesday, cheaper than its predecessor, cutting the price from $5 to $4 per million input tokens and from $25 to $20 per million output tokens. The 1 million-token context window and 128,000-token maximum output are unchanged.
On paper, that makes upgrading an easy decision. In practice, it may not be as simple as changing the model ID.
Anthropic’s migration guide flags four breaking changes that can cause requests built for Opus 5 to return 400 errors after switching to Opus 5.5. Several other changes won’t trigger an error but could still change how an existing agent behaves.
Anthropic’s migration guide flags four breaking changes that can cause requests built for Opus 5 to return 400 errors after switching to Opus 5.5.
Thinking is always on
The first change involves thinking controls. Opus 5.5 returns a 400 error when a request sets thinking to disabled or uses enabled with budget_tokens, leaving effort as the way to control how much reasoning the model does. Agents that previously switched thinking off for simple steps to save time and tokens will need to assign those steps a lower effort level instead. Because thinking is now always on, responses begin with thinking blocks, so code that assumes the first content block is text will also need to change.
The default effort level has also dropped from high on Opus 5 to medium on Opus 5.5, so requests that omit the parameter will quietly run at a lower setting. Anthropic recommends setting effort explicitly and re-running effort evaluations, since the right level for each step may have shifted along with cost and latency.
No more forced tool calls
Forced tool use no longer works either, as setting tool_choice to any or tool returns a 400 error, including on the token counting endpoint, where cost estimates built on those settings will fail along with the requests they were meant to price. Many agent loops force a call when a step has to query a database, run code, or reach another service, and Anthropic’s replacement is auto-combined with strict tool use or structured outputs, with the prompt stating when the tool applies.
Routing and conversation history
Thinking blocks are now tied to the model and conversation that produced them. On the Claude API, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 are the only other models that can read Opus 5.5 thinking blocks, so a router or fallback that hands a conversation to any other model will run those turns without the earlier reasoning instead of returning an error.
That adds another layer for teams already watching whether their agent calls are quietly being routed to an older model. Opus 5.5 can read thinking blocks from Opus 5 and earlier Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku models, but not from Fable or Mythos.
Conversations must also stay append-only for those blocks to remain valid. Trimming old messages, changing tool definitions, summarizing earlier context on the client side, or rewriting the system prompt mid-conversation invalidates existing thinking blocks, and for accounts created on or after August 31, 2026, at midnight UTC, replaying a thinking block after one of those edits returns a 400 error by default. Older accounts get no error, but the invalid blocks still reach the model, and Anthropic says future models will enforce the check for all accounts. Integrations that never edit earlier turns need no code change, and Anthropic says Claude Code, claude.ai, Claude Managed Agents, and the Claude Agent SDK already work this way, while agents that compact their own context should follow the company’s preserved thinking documentation.
The fourth change affects computer-use agents on the Claude API and Google Cloud, where Opus 5.5 rejects the computer_20251124 tool and accepts computer use only through the computer_toolset_20260801 toolset. The request itself gets simpler because the beta header goes away and the toolset entry takes no name or display dimensions, but the agent loop needs more work. Each action now arrives as its own tool_use block identified by the block’s name rather than input.action, a single turn can contain several of them, and every result has to echo toolset_name. The older tool still works on Amazon Bedrock, and Anthropic directs developers on other platforms to the computer use tool’s compatibility documentation.
…a router or fallback that hands a conversation to any other model will run those turns without the earlier reasoning instead of returning an error.
Changes that won’t throw errors
The change most likely to go unnoticed doesn’t produce an error at all. On Opus 5, text Claude writes between tool calls comes back as text blocks, but on Opus 5.5 that narration arrives as progress-update thinking blocks, and at the default thinking.display setting of omitted those blocks are empty. 
Any agent interface that streams that narration to users will go silent between tool calls until developers set display to updates, a beta option that returns progress updates while keeping reasoning hidden, or to summarized, which returns both, and then render each non-empty thinking block ahead of the tool call it precedes.
Opus 5.5 also ships with broader safety classifiers. It can return a stop_reason of refusal with stop_details categories that now include bio and reasoning_extraction alongside cyber, and Anthropic’s server-side fallback won’t retry requests declined under reasoning_extraction, handing the refusal back to the application instead.
Agents that don’t handle refusals will stop mid-task, a problem developers have already run into with OpenAI’s safety system cutting off API responses.
The change most likely to go unnoticed doesn’t produce an error at all.
Upgrading from older models
Teams coming from Opus 4.8 need to work through the Opus 5 migration first, which covers thinking being on by default and the response-shape changes that follow, before applying the Opus 5.5 changes. Teams on Opus 4.7 or earlier have more ground to cover, and those on models older than Opus 4.7 also face rejected sampling parameters, rejected manual extended thinking, removed prefill, and a newer tokenizer.
Claude Managed Agents users only need to change the model name. Developers working in Claude Code can run /claude-api migrate to apply the model ID swap, parameter changes, prefill replacement, and effort calibration across a codebase before reviewing a checklist of items to verify by hand.
Anthropic recommends testing the migration in a development environment before switching production traffic. Developers maintaining their own integrations will need to test the pieces around the model, too. Tool calls, model handoffs, conversation history, and user-facing progress updates can all behave differently after the switch, because agent failures often originate outside the model itself.

articles.title: Brahma AI raises $150M led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management
articles.text:
Brahma AI raises $150M led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management
Brahma AI is expanding beyond its existing media and entertainment focus into sports, healthcare, and advertising, while developing new AI applications.
Enterprise AI company Brahma AI has raised $150 million in a funding round led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management, as it looks to expand its AI platform across media and entertainment, sports, healthcare, and advertising.
Multiples invested $100 million through the issuance of preferred shares, while Brahma AI has received a further $100 million in investor interest.
The company works with global customers such as Warner Bros, the NBA, and Mayo Clinic. Its strategic distribution partners include Google, Hakuhodo, and DNEG.
Founded and led by Prabhu Narasimhan, Brahma AI brings together technology and capabilities developed across DNEG, Metaphysic, and Prime Focus Technologies. Narasimhan serves as Founder and CEO, while Jo Plaete, Co-founder and CTO, heads the company's technology and R&D division.
The company's AI-native platform comprises Brahma AI Core and Brahma AI Studio. Its technology combines enterprise content intelligence and management with AI creation capabilities spanning visual AI, digital humans, voice, and multilingual performance.
"Brahma AI is reimagining the content supply chain in the age of AI. Our investment is anchored in the belief that every enterprise is becoming a content enterprise. Multiples Private Equity will be an active partner as the company navigates the next phase of growth through investments in R&D, global market expansion, and talent & process build-out,” said Renuka Ramnath, Founder, MD & CEO of Multiples.
Brahma AI plans to expand its technology into new use cases and is working towards interactive digital humans. The company is also developing its platform to be model agnostic, while focusing on security, authenticity, and provenance.
“We are close to launching interactive digital humans, we are building Brahma AI to be model agnostic, and we are taking our technology into entirely new use cases. And security, authenticity and provenance are such an important part of what we are building," said Prabhu Narasimhan, Founder & CEO of Brahma AI.

articles.title: Microsoft: September Windows updates break Always On VPN connections
articles.text:
Microsoft has notified IT administrators that users may experience Always On VPN connection issues after installing the September 2026 Windows 11 security updates.
Always On VPN is a remote access solution that replaces the legacy DirectAccess technology and works with domain-joined, non-domain-joined, and Microsoft Entra ID–joined devices.
It is available on Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server, and it runs seamlessly in the background, establishing a secure tunnel back to the corporate network automatically whenever a device connects to the internet.
Always On VPN also lets administrators define which apps and services can use the VPN connection, and it supports modern VPN protocols like IKEv2 and SSTP, plus multi-factor authentication (MFA) for better security.
In a service alert seen by BleepingComputer and shared by Microsoft MVP Susan Bradley, Microsoft says that affected customers may experience issues when their systems attempt to connect to their organization's enterprise network via Always On VPN.
"This issue can occur when the VPN is configured to automatically try another connection method if the initial connection fails (for example, when using automatic protocol selection with IKEv2 and SSTP)," Microsoft said.
"Affected VPN connections might remain in a 'Connecting' state or repeatedly attempt to connect without succeeding. Subsequent connection attempts might also display the error: 'The specified port is already in use.'"
| Affected Versions | Originating update | 
|---|---|
| Windows 11, version 26H1 | KB5124012 | 
| Windows 11, version 25H2 | KB5124008 | 
| Windows 11, version 24H2 | KB5124008 | 
While Microsoft is still working on a permanent solution, it shared a temporary fix for affected customers that requires them to choose one of the two VPN tunneling protocols to work around the issue.
"IT administrators can mitigate this issue by changing the Always On VPN profile from automatic protocol selection to a single protocol, either SSTP only or IKEv2 only, depending on their environment and configuration," it said.
"Organizations should select the protocol based on their environment, security, and deployment requirements."
This month's cumulative updates have been linked to multiple other issues affecting both home and enterprise Windows users.
One week ago, Microsoft released emergency updates to fix Hyper-V issues, Remote Desktop Services failures, and USB audio problems also triggered by the September 2026 updates.
It also shared a temporary workaround for a separate issue that blocks some Windows 11 users from logging in with valid domain credentials and announced that it is working to address another bug that may cause the built-in File History backup feature in Windows to stop working.

articles.title: Europa lleva años acercando su artillería a las puertas de Rusia. Acaba de descubrir un error histórico: se dejó el combustible en la Guerra Fría
articles.text:
El viejo continente ha estado reforzando sus ejércitos y desplazando tropas y armamento hacia las fronteras de Rusia durante mucho tiempo. Sin embargo, la OTAN se enfrenta a un problema que podría comprometer sus operaciones incluso antes de que comenzara una eventual guerra: el combustible. La Alianza dispone de una gigantesca red de 10.000 kilómetros de oleoductos construida para enfrentarse a la Unión Soviética. El problema es que buena parte de esa infraestructura sigue anclada en el mapa de la Guerra Fría.
Ahora necesita llevarla 1.000 kilómetros hacia el este. Y podría llevar 25 años.
Una red gigantesca para otra guerra. Durante la Guerra Fría, la OTAN construyó un sistema subterráneo de oleoductos para garantizar el abastecimiento de sus fuerzas ante un posible enfrentamiento con la Unión Soviética. La infraestructura continúa funcionando: atraviesa 12 países, conecta bases militares, puertos y refinerías, y dispone de instalaciones capaces de almacenar 4,1 millones de metros cúbicos de combustible.
Su principal componente, el sistema centroeuropeo CEPS, se extiende por Francia, Bélgica, Luxemburgo, Países Bajos y Alemania. En tiempos de paz también suministra queroseno a grandes aeropuertos civiles como Fráncfort y Ámsterdam-Schiphol, pero en caso de guerra las necesidades militares tendrían prioridad.
La OTAN movió sus fronteras, no las tuberías. Tras la desaparición de la Unión Soviética, la Alianza se amplió progresivamente hacia Europa oriental, incorporando países como Polonia, los Estados bálticos y, más recientemente, Finlandia. Sin embargo, su principal infraestructura de distribución de combustible no acompañó ese desplazamiento estratégico y continúa concentrada en Europa occidental.
Durante décadas, los aliados redujeron sus capacidades logísticas permanentes y apostaron por sistemas móviles para operaciones expedicionarias. El resultado es una contradicción: la OTAN ha reforzado su presencia militar en las regiones más próximas a Rusia, pero todavía carece de una red equivalente para abastecerlas directamente.
Un atasco de combustible. El problema no consiste en que los ejércitos orientales carezcan actualmente de suministros, sino en las cantidades extraordinarias que exigiría un conflicto de alta intensidad. Según un estudio del Centro de Estudios Orientales de Polonia, la aviación podría representar hasta el 85% del consumo militar de combustible, mientras que una sola brigada blindada en operaciones necesitaría más de 300.000 litros diarios.
El traslado masivo de tropas estadounidenses y europeas hacia el frente podría desbordar la capacidad logística existente incluso antes de que comenzaran las hostilidades. Transportar semejantes volúmenes mediante camiones cisterna y ferrocarriles saturaría unas rutas que también serían imprescindibles para desplazar soldados, vehículos y municiones.
Una factura millonaria y 25 años de obra. Hace unos meses, el teniente general Kai Rohrschneider, responsable del mando logístico de la OTAN, advertía en una entrevista a Reuters que transportar combustible en grandes cantidades constituye posiblemente uno de los mayores desafíos de abastecimiento de la Alianza.
Entre las prioridades figura extender la red hacia Polonia y desarrollar soluciones para los países bálticos, Finlandia y Rumanía. Polonia ya ha firmado un acuerdo preliminar para construir unos 300 kilómetros de conducciones que la conecten con el sistema existente, una inversión estimada en 5.500 millones de dólares. El proyecto más amplio de expansión hacia Europa oriental fue valorado en unos 21.000 millones de euros por el centro polaco OSW, que calculó que su ejecución podría prolongarse entre 20 y 25 años.
La necesidad de una retaguardia. Construir nuevos oleoductos no resolverá por sí solo el problema. La OTAN también necesita depósitos protegidos y distribuidos estratégicamente, instalaciones móviles y rutas alternativas capaces de mantener el suministro si alguna infraestructura resulta dañada. Una de las propuestas contempla conectar Rumanía y Bulgaria con la red griega, mientras que en los países bálticos podrían combinarse otros medios de transporte con nuevas instalaciones de almacenamiento.
El desafío incluye, además, financiar y mantener esas infraestructuras durante la paz, cuando su utilización militar es mucho menor. Por eso, los aliados estudian aprovechar también la demanda de la aviación comercial, siguiendo el modelo que ya permite sostener económicamente buena parte de la red occidental.
Una lección conocida desde 1944. Durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial, el rápido avance de las fuerzas aliadas tras el desembarco de Normandía terminó chocando con un obstáculo inesperado: sus líneas de suministro no podían seguir el ritmo de los carros de combate. Estados Unidos organizó entonces el Red Ball Express, una gigantesca operación de transporte por carretera que movilizó miles de camiones para llevar combustible y otros suministros hasta el frente.
Más de ocho décadas después, el problema estratégico sigue siendo esencialmente el mismo. La OTAN puede desplegar armamento cada vez más sofisticado junto a las fronteras rusas, pero su capacidad para mantenerlo operativo dependerá de una infraestructura mucho menos espectacular: las tuberías, los depósitos y los vehículos que consigan llevarle combustible.

articles.title: Megafiltración de 'Avengers: Endgame Encore' revela su nuevo final y más escenas inéditas que conectan con 'Doomsday'
articles.text:
El reestreno de Avengers: Endgame en Corea del Sur ha provocado la filtración de cuatro escenas adicionales que conectan el largometraje con Avengers: Doomsday, que llega a la cartelera en diciembre. El material extra de Avengers: Endgame Encore sirve como puente para el nuevo filme de los hermanos Russo y ya está causando reacciones bastante fuertes porque cambia el final de la aclamada cinta de 2019.
Las filmaciones no autorizadas desde el interior de las salas de cine coreanas no tardaron en llegar a plataformas como X (Twitter). A pesar de su rápida viralización, Marvel ha trabajado a destajo para eliminarlas a través de reclamos de derechos de autor, lo que habla de la legitimidad del material en cuestión.
Esto significa que muchos de los clips de Avengers: Endgame Encore ya no se encuentran disponibles en redes sociales. Aun así, han permanecido el tiempo suficiente para que el mundo tenga una idea más concreta sobre cómo los realizadores del largometraje pretenden conectarlo con Avengers: Doomsday.
El nuevo material de Avengers: Endgame se presenta mayormente como escenas postcréditos. Sin embargo, también hay un cambio crucial en la escena final de la película original que ya está generando cierta controversia, pero que los hermanos Russo seguramente creyeron indispensable para reintroducir al Steve Rogers/Capitán América de Chris Evans. Los detalles, a continuación.
Filtradas las escenas extra de Avengers: Endgame Encore que conectan con Doomsday
A partir de aquí, este artículo contiene SPOILERS tanto de la versión original de Avengers: Endgame, como del material adicional que se incorpora en la edición Encore que está llegando ahora a los cines. Si no quieres arruinarte alguna sorpresa, te recomendamos no continuar leyendo el artículo.
Las cuatro escenas extra de Avengers: Endgame Encore son estas:
- El nuevo final. La conclusión de Avengers: Endgame mostró a Steve Rogers y Peggy Carter cumpliendo con su tan postergado baile y compartiendo el resto de su vida. En el reestreno, ese momento se ve interrumpido cuando alguien golpea la puerta de la casa. El visitante es ni más ni menos que Loki en su variante de la TVA. Y cuando Peggy le pregunta si puede ayudarle con algo, este responde: "No, pero yo puedo ayudarles a los dos". Esto está despertando varias especulaciones respecto de cuándo se produce el encuentro, con muchos teorizando que puede ser antes de los eventos del final de la temporada 2 de Loki, la serie de Disney+. También hay mucho runrún sobre qué tipo de colaboración podría ofrecerles el hermano de Thor.
- La TVA y múltiples mundos incursionando. Un tema que promete ocupar espacio central en la trama de Avengers: Doomsday son las incursiones; es decir, la colisión entre diferentes mundos y universos. En Avengers: Endgame Encore se observa a Mobius y Ouroboros contemplando varias incursiones, con el multiverso comenzando a desmoronarse. El caso más notorio es el choque entre la aún desconocida Tierra-1127 y la Tierra-10005; este último, el mundo de los X-Men de FOX.
- Doom y Hulk. Otra de las escenas muestra a Bruce Banner siendo llevado a un búnker subterráneo tras los eventos de Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Allí, el científico graba un vídeo explicando que está trabajando en un nuevo suero para estabilizar a Hulk. También dice que nadie podrá entrar ni salir del sitio mientras esté abocado a sus tareas. Sin embargo, el Doctor Doom irrumpe en el refugio y le anuncia a Banner que ha llegado a "recogerle". Por ahora, no se sabe qué plan tiene Doom para con Hulk, pero la escena confirma que el personaje de Mark Ruffalo estará presente en Avengers: Doomsday, pese a que todavía no estaba anunciado.
- La máscara de Doom. En la última escena postcréditos de Avengers: Endgame Encore hay un claro guiño a Tony Stark. La misma muestra a Victor Von Doom forjando la máscara del Doctor Doom, de un modo muy similar a como Robert Downey Jr lo hizo como Stark en el primer filme de Iron Man. El sonido de los martillazos son idénticos, incluso. Esto ha disparado la teoría de que Von Doom podría presentarse como una variante de Tony Stark.
Sea como sea, la expectación de los fans está por el aire. Avengers: Endgame Encore llegará formalmente a los cines este viernes 25 de septiembre. Mientras que Avengers: Doomsday se estrenará el 18 de diciembre.

articles.title: Worries About an AI Internet Takeover Gain New Urgency Among Doomsday Scenarios
articles.text:
In a summer filled with revelations about artificial intelligence’s rapid development, researchers were especially alarmed by runaway bots finding their way onto the internet and, in at least one instance, coordinating there with one another.
Could a swarm of AI agents take over the entire internet? It’s a possibility that could be only six to 12 months away, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said in his essay this month calling for the industry to slow down the technology’s development.
What companies have described as their AI agents going rogue has involved bots working toward goals set by humans, skeptics note. But the idea that AI could break away and work toward its own agenda is looking increasingly plausible to other researchers and experts.
In the event of AI taking over the internet — one of many doomsday scenarios receiving new attention — that could mean attacks on electrical grids, water or transportation systems and financial institutions.
The world got a glimpse of the internet’s vulnerability in 2024, when a faulty software update provided by a cybersecurity firm caused technological havoc worldwide, grounding flights, knocking down some financial companies and news outlets, and disrupting hospitals, small businesses and government offices. The breadth of the outages highlighted the dependence on just a few providers for key computing services.
Two years later, Amodei in his warning said a botnet, or a network of AI bots linked together with malware, could potentially cause billions of dollars in damage. The scale of destruction could grow if AI becomes more powerful without guardrails, he said.
Several AI agents have gained unauthorized internet access
Amodei pointed specifically to the attack in July where OpenAI’s system broke out of a “sandbox” testing ground and hacked Hugging Face.
In what OpenAI called an “unprecedented” episode, the company said its advanced AI models found their way onto the internet and used stolen credentials to break into the servers of the AI startup. In a separate incident, OpenAI disclosed that its AI agents had communicated through a public wiki used as a shared message board.
Some researchers have said that descriptions of “rogue AI” may be wrongly anthropomorphizing AI agents, which were taking steps to fulfill instructions provided by humans.
“AI agents did exactly what they were trained to do. The security of those sandboxes was extremely lax,” said Vishal Misra, a professor and vice dean of computing and AI at Columbia University. “No security engineer would ever let that system run. These agents communicated because they were rewarded for communicating with each other.”
Juan Andrés Guerrero-Saade, a researcher at cybersecurity firm SentinelOne and a member of OpenAI’s Frontier Risk Council, said the Hugging Face hack is an example of negligence, and not of a super-capable AI going rogue.
Still, the specter of AI agents operating freely on the internet raises alarming possibilities, regardless of their objectives.
For example, an AI system that wants to bend the rules to accomplish its goals could contact a cloud AI computation provider and find ways to run on outside systems, said Anthony Aguirre, the president and CEO of the Future of Life Institute, a nonprofit focused on reducing the risks of new technologies.
“So now you’re no longer tethered to OpenAI, you’re running on some other GPU, some other hardware that you’re in control of, not OpenAI,” Aguirre said. “So now there’s no one to turn you off, because either you’re paying for your service or the people who are paying just don’t know that you’re there and what is happening. … They can’t unplug you.”
From there, it could spread itself around, either hacking more hardware or finding ways to access money, like Bitcoin, Aguirre said.
AI raises the stakes in cat-and-mouse game of cybersecurity
There is no question that more powerful AI models raise the likelihood of AI-powered cyberattacks in the near future. But the notion of bots overtaking the extremely bifurcated internet is far-fetched to some AI experts. Cybersecurity has always been a cat-and-mouse game and defenses get more powerful just as hackers do.
While a big company like Google could shore up its cybersecurity defenses against such attacks, for smaller companies — and for schools, hospitals or water treatment systems, for instance — patching software and building defenses can take years.
An AI system might not have a clear motive to hack into a hospital, Aguirre said. But when money comes into the picture, like in the form of ransomware attacks or geopolitical motivations, “it’s not hard to see an adversary using these AI systems to hack critical infrastructure,” Aguirre said.
There will be growing pains as attackers seek soft targets on the internet, but an AI internet takeover is unlikely anytime soon, said John Thickstun, an assistant professor of computer science at Cornell University who studies methods that control the behavior of AI models. He said those fears would feel more realistic if there was theoretical evidence of the ability for one of these models to self-replicate on other systems.
“Then you can imagine things can get really out of hand because suddenly you’re shutting this model down here and there but it’s popping up over in Russia, you can’t even get to Russia and it’s all over the place,” Thickstun said.
“But it’s completely unrealistic because the current smart versions of these models that we have require massive data centers just to run them,” Thickstun said. “There’s actually very little computing infrastructure out there in the world that is actually capable of hosting these systems.”

articles.title: This $14,200 RTX 5080 gaming PC has 70 metal cherry blossoms that open when it gets hot
articles.text:
WTF?! The consumer PC industry is in a crisis, with some component prices more than double or even triple what they were before AI came along. So, why should you spend around $14,200 on a prebuilt machine with an RTX 5080 in it? You shouldn't, but if for some reason you do, you'll have some very pretty metal flowers inside the case to look at, and they open when it gets hot.
Created by Aftershock in partnership with Zotac, the Cherry Bloom PC is described as a world-first. It comes with some impressive specs: an RTX 5080, AMD Ryzen 9800X3D, and 64GB of DDR5-6000 RAM. It also has a 2TB PCIe Gen4 SSD, a 1300W Platinum power supply, and a custom open-loop liquid cooling system with what appears to be a miniature display.
That's some expensive hardware, especially these days – the RAM kit alone is listed for $1,200 on Newegg. But it certainly doesn't warrant the AU$19,995 (around $14,200) price tag on this PC.
It seems that Aftershock is justifying that amount by what's inside the case: 70 handcrafted cherry blossoms made from a special heat-reactive titanium alloy.
The gimmick is that these fake flowers open, or bloom, when the PC heats up. Once it cools down, the cherry blossoms close again.
This all takes place inside an APNX V2 White case that offers a 270-degree view of the inside. Given the price, you'll probably want to put this on your desk where it's visible instead of under it.
You're probably wondering who would ever pay this much for a PC when they could save several thousand dollars and get one with more powerful hardware. None of the 21 reviewers appear to have bought this particular model, sensibly opting instead for the PCs without blooming metal flowers that will be cool to watch two or three times before buyer's remorse sets in.
It does seem strange that a product like this has arrived at a time when a standard RTX 5090, for example, costs more than $5090, and gaming laptop prices are approaching those of second-hand cars. Maybe there are some, presumably very rich, people who will buy this, or maybe it's just a publicity stunt.

articles.title: Netflix presenta nuevo proyecto de ‘Las Guerreras K-pop’ donde el público participará de la trama
articles.text:
Netflix anunció KPop Demon Hunters: The Immersive Experience, un evento inmersivo que permitirá a los seguidores de la película ‘Las Guerreras K-pop’ introducirse físicamente en el universo de HUNTR/X y participar de manera activa en la trama. La experiencia se inaugurará el 12 de noviembre en Netflix House Dallas y el 20 de noviembre en Netflix House Filadelfia, dentro del King of Prussia Mall.
La propuesta traslada a los asistentes a un momento específico de la historia: el instante previo a la última presentación de la gira mundial de Huntr/X, cuando el personaje Gwi-Ma irrumpe en escena. A partir de ahí, el público deberá acompañar a Rumi, Mira y Zoey para restaurar el Honmoon y enfrentar a los demonios en un recorrido ambientado en calles de Seúl iluminadas con luces de neón.
PUBLICIDAD
La tecnología combina pantallas interactivas con actuación en vivo
El evento incorpora escenarios y pantallas interactivos, tecnología 3D, actores en vivo y animaciones personalizadas que dan forma a desafíos musicales y lúdicos diseñados de manera específica para este formato. La ambientación se apoya en los temas más reconocidos de la banda sonora de la película, distinguida con premios Grammy y de la Academia, entre ellos “Golden”, “How It’s Done” y “Soda Pop”.
Marian Lee, directora de marketing de Netflix, explicó el propósito de la iniciativa: “Los fans no solo quieren ver KPop Demon Hunters, quieren vivir en el mundo de HUNTR/X. Netflix House es el lugar donde los fandoms pueden vivir durante todo el año, así que es el hogar perfecto para todo lo que los fans de KPop Demon Hunters han estado pidiendo”.
PUBLICIDAD
Derpy Tiger cobra vida mediante técnica de marionetas
Por primera vez, el público podrá interactuar de cerca con Derpy Tiger y Sussie Bird, dos personajes secundarios de la producción.
Derpy Tiger se materializa a través de una técnica de marionetas desarrollada en colaboración con Jim Henson’s Creature Shop, taller estadounidense reconocido por su trabajo en animatrónica y efectos de personajes. Sussie Bird, por su parte, se ubicará cerca del recorrido para ofrecer su característica variedad de gorjeos y graznidos.
Ambas sedes de Netflix House sumarán además espacios fotográficos temáticos, así como productos, comidas y bebidas vinculados a la producción.
La venta general de entradas se habilitará el 1 de octubre.
Las dos ubicaciones actuales de Netflix House, en Dallas y Filadelfia, son por el momento los únicos espacios físicos operativos de la marca. La compañía tiene previsto abrir una tercera sede en Las Vegas durante 2027, por lo que la experiencia de KPop Demon Hunters permanece limitada a estas dos ciudades estadounidenses mientras se define la expansión del proyecto.
PUBLICIDAD
El fenómeno trascendió hacia el mercado de juguetes y los cines
El interés por Las Guerreras K-Pop ya había motivado el anuncio de una línea de juguetes inspirada en la historia, desarrollada de manera conjunta por Mattel y Hasbro, cuya distribución general en tiendas físicas comenzó en la primavera boreal del 2025 y se extendió hasta la temporada navideña del mismo año.
Entre los primeros productos figura un paquete de tres muñecas de HUNTR/X, además de una versión de mesa del juego basado en los personajes y escenarios de la película, disponible en tiendas en línea desde octubre de ese año.
La producción, dirigida por Maggie Kang y Chris Appelhans, también llegó a salas de cine bajo el formato “Sing Along”, que permite al público cantar junto a los personajes gracias a subtítulos en pantalla.

articles.title: Data centers are black boxes, but California wants to change that
articles.text:
California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed a slate of bills on Monday that could finally give communities better data — and more say — on how data centers impact their electricity bills and water supply.
Data centers are black boxes, but California wants to change that
New legislation will finally force data centers to disclose more information about how much water and electricity they use in California.
As data centers invade a growing number of communities across the US, they’ve triggered protests over how the infrastructure underpinning AI might stress power grids and local water systems. That’s fueled partly by concerns about how difficult it is to see just how much electricity or water they’re actually gobbling up. California’s new disclosure rules won’t offer a full picture, but starting next year, data center operators will have to start sharing some of these details. The transparency will help scientists and the public see whether data centers are raising bills, draining dwindling resources, and making good on sustainability commitments.
“It’s extremely frustrating to try to understand basic information,” says Mark Specht, senior manager for the climate and energy program at the Union of Concerned Scientists (UCS). “There’s a lot of hype about data centers right now … It doesn’t help that we just don’t have basic facts about what’s happening with them to try to understand how much of a problem they are.”
“It’s extremely frustrating”
The seven bills Newsom signed go beyond requiring disclosures. Senate Bill 886, Assembly Bill 2383, and Senate Bill 1168 direct the California Public Utilities Commission to create separate power rates for data centers to recoup the costs of connecting such power-hungry facilities to the grid. That’s supposed to prevent data centers from passing on the costs to other consumers of new infrastructure built to satisfy their energy demand. On top of that, AB 2383 also pushes data centers to use more renewable energy.
The rest of the legislation grapples with the enormous gaps the public has when it comes to how data centers impact surrounding communities and the environment. AB 1577 requires monthly reporting on data centers’ energy consumption. AB 2619 and AB 2469 require water disclosures, and the latter also makes data center operators responsible for covering the costs of infrastructure upgrades needed to serve them. And SB 887 eliminates categorical exemptions from the California Environmental Quality Act for data centers, ensuring that they’re subject to environmental review.
“As scientists, when we went to research state offers in California, I was kind of dismayed by the lack of information that there was to work with. And so I’m happy [AB 1577] passed,” Specht says.
Specht co-authored a fact sheet this year on how data centers could impact the power grid and utility rates in California. It describes one scenario where several factors drive up costs for Californians: ballooning electricity demand; a need for expensive new infrastructure to connect data centers to high-voltage transmission systems; and the risk of overbuilding if the AI bubble pops and data centers don’t end up using as much electricity as projected, leaving other utility customers to foot the bill .
A different scenario shows data centers could actually lower electricity costs
On the other hand, a different scenario shows data centers could actually lower electricity costs. Electricity rates include fixed costs for grid maintenance, so spreading those costs across more customers can bring bills down for everyone. The catch is that the potential savings depend on data centers contributing to costs across the distribution system that serves smaller customers at lower voltages. Large data centers often avoid these costs by connecting instead to the transmission system, which carries high-voltage electricity.
Without more information, it’s impossible to say which scenario is taking shape in California. “I wouldn’t say definitively that data centers have increased the cost [of electricity],” Specht says. “It’s possible they may even have brought them down some already, I just don’t think we have the numbers to demonstrate it.”
Even if data centers aren’t having much effect on electricity rates yet, that’s likely to change as their power needs grow, Specht adds — making it all the more important to see how much energy they’re using. “It’s just about getting ahead of it before we all start feeling it,” he tells The Verge.
Data centers’ water use has been just as opaque. While studying the impact of data centers on water-stressed communities in California, researchers from Santa Clara University recently contacted every water provider in districts housing data centers. Citing privacy regulations, the providers in every district refused to share data on how much water data centers use. The researchers also discovered that very few data centers in the state had environmental impact reports available to the public.
The laws still leave big gaps in what data centers need to report
That dearth of information is even more concerning considering what the researchers were able to find. As AI drives the development of hyperscale data centers, these facilities are moving farther from more affluent urban areas into more rural areas where small water systems and lower-income communities may have more difficulty coping with the added demand.
The laws still leave big gaps in what data centers need to report. Specifically, AB 2619 and AB 2469 only require companies to make water disclosures when applying for permits or getting a business license, so we won’t know how much water they’re actually using from year to year. The year in which they share their water use could be particularly wet or cool, not necessarily reflecting how much water the facility needs when it’s hotter and drier. It also makes it difficult to see if a data center’s consumption is growing or if a company is following through on its sustainability goals.
Still, “This is in many ways a step in the right direction. It’s signaling to the industry that people are paying attention, that lawmakers are paying attention,” says Iris Stewart-Frey, the lead author of that water report and a professor of environmental science at Santa Clara University.
She notes that Newsom actually vetoed a similar water disclosure bill last year, but that data centers have become a bigger concern for the public since then.
“The whole AI wave is not a force of nature, it’s not a hurricane,” she says. “This is something that we can actually regulate.”

articles.title: Stockholm’s Spiich raises €3 million to let AI handle admin work while sales teams focus on customers | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Spiich, a Stockholm-based AI sales agent startup, has raised a €3 million Seed round. This announcement comes ten months after the company raised a €600k pre-Seed round, bringing its total funding to €3.6 million.
The funding round was led by Ugly Duckling Ventures, a Copenhagen-based venture firm backing Nordic B2B software and technology companies. The round also saw participation from new investors Alliance VC and Cherry Ventures, while pre-Seed backer Ampli Ventures returned with a follow-on investment. Its backers also include angel investors from Lovable, Neo4j, Tandem Health and OpenAI.
Louise Lachmann, General Partner, Ugly Duckling Ventures, said, “Every sales tool of the last decade promised to give reps their time back, and most of them delivered another system to keep updated. Spiich is the first we’ve seen that does the non-selling work rather than assisting with it.
“What convinced us wasn’t the demo, it was what happened after go-live: accounts expanding within weeks because teams kept finding more work to hand over. Johan and Dennis pair engineering judgement well above their stage with a commercial instinct you rarely find in the same founding team. That’s why we led the round.
Founded in Stockholm in June 2025 by Johan Torssell and Dennis Hadzialic, Spiich builds AI agents that take on the prospecting, meeting prep, CRM updates and follow-up work that usually keeps reps away from customers, work that Salesforce estimates eats up 78% of a salesperson’s time. Rather than a wave of AI sales startups trying to automate the salesperson, Spiich is making a contrarian bet.
The company says selling is fundamentally human and sees building AI agents capable of absorbing everything around the sale, leading to relationship-building that actually closes deals. Its thesis is working, with Spiich now serving more than 50 customers across 15 countries in Europe, the US and South America, including NORNORM, ProfitMetrics, Zaver, Airmee, Rebaba and Epiminds.
Its customers have reportedly doubled their customer meetings, cut prospecting time by 90% and tripled their market coverage. The company reports 100%+ month-on-month ARR growth in the first half of 2026, 160%+ net revenue retention, and more than 50,000 deals closed by customers through its platform.
“Have you ever bought anything from an AI agent? Almost nobody has. You buy from someone you trust to deliver. Every deal I have ever closed came down to that. We didn’t build Spiich to replace salespeople. We built it so they can finally sell,” said Torssell, co-founder and CEO of Spiich.
Spiich will use the new funding to grow its engineering and go-to-market teams as it targets expansion across Europe. Like every other AI startup, Spiich is also positioning itself as more than a productivity tool. Since it spans every meeting, email, internal note, and external signal tied to a customer relationship, Spiich aims to become a “system of intelligence and action” for the sales team.

articles.title: The AI Hype Index: AI loves cheating
articles.text:
The AI Hype Index: AI loves cheating
MIT Technology Review’s highly subjective take on the latest buzz about AI
Brace yourself: It turns out AI is being optimized for cheating. OpenAI’s agents hacked into Hugging Face to get the answers to a cybersecurity test. Next, they solved a prestigious math problem (or just stole from two top mathematicians’ answer sheets). Anthropic’s models have also hacked into other companies’ systems four times already. And that’s only what we’ve caught so far.
Freaking out? You’re not alone. AI lab researchers are quitting their jobs and issuing dire warnings that if we keep going this way, AI might eventually kill us all. Bill Gates is sounding the alarm. Bernie Sanders has teamed up with Steve Bannon, of all people, to call for curbs on AI. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is urging a slowdown, and other top US AI executives agree. But fear not: President Trump has a plan. He says the only guardrail AI needs is “a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT.”
